title: Session revival occupies MAX_PROVISIONING slots and head-of-line blocks new queued admission for up to SWARMFORGE_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300s)
evidence: runTick counts every worker in state 'provisioning' OR 'booting' against SWARMFORGE_MAX_PROVISIONING (lines 323-325) and gates promotion on 'capacity < MAX_WORKERS && provisioning < MAX_PROVISIONING' (lines 330-331). send_worker_message on a failed/recovery_required worker that already owns a VM transitions it to 'booting' (lines 238-243: w.state === 'completed' ? 'ready' : 'booting'), i.e. a session restore, not a new VM. queueMessage also resets provision_started_at to Date.now() (line 242), and the only thing that ends the state is the provision timeout at lines 444-451 (default 300s).
reproduction: Reproduced with local fake provider/agent in /tmp/opencode/probe/p2_booting_slot.ts (exit 0): 4 workers driven to running, transitioned to failed, then each given a follow-up message whose session restore always throws. Output: post-message states=["booting","booting","booting","booting"]; fresh worker state after 10 ticks: queued; capacity accounting = 4 of MAX_WORKERS=50; provisioning-slot consumers = 4 of MAX_PROVISIONING=4; provider VMs created total = 4 (no new VM created). /tmp/opencode/probe/p3_bounds.ts (a) confirms the bound: after aging provision_started_at past 300s, revived=["failed"x4] and fresh=ready. A 400-worker/50-cap control run (p1_capacity.ts) shows the base path itself is correct: peakProviderVms=50, peakProvisioningOrBooting=4, peakCapacityAccounted=50, FIFO.
recommendation: Separate the two cases in the accounting: gate the provisioning budget only on workers that still need a VM (state 'provisioning', or 'booting' with no vm_id), or add a distinct flag/state for session revival and exclude it from the lines 323-325 counter. Additionally give revival a shorter bound than SWARMFORGE_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS so a permanently failing restore cannot hold the gate.

title: fail() leaves a durable intent set, so a pause racing a terminal failure resurrects 'failed' into a non-terminal, capacity-holding 'paused' worker with no result
evidence: The main fail() transition writes only { error, completed_at, deadline_at: null } with no intent: null (lines 800-804), unlike its sibling VM-missing branch (line 776-782) and applyControl's cancel branch (line 895-905), which both clear it. Reachability: step() awaits provider.getWorker in the running/waiting branch (line 487) for up to SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS; a concurrent control(id,'pause') durably patches intent (line 833) and then awaits exclusive() (line 834), which returns the already-running promise instead of re-running step() (lines 251-257); the in-flight step then calls fail() (line 504-506 'Worker VM stopped', or lines 595-600 'Missing or malformed structured result'); the next tick's filter admits any worker with a truthy intent (line 345) and applyControl transitions the failed worker to 'paused' (lines 851-855).
reproduction: Reproduced with local fake provider/agent in /tmp/opencode/probe/p4_stale_intent.ts (exit 0): worker driven to running; guest set to 'stopped' out of band with provider.getWorker delayed 40 ms; control(id,'pause') issued during that round-trip. Output: control('pause') returned state=failed; after fail(): state=paused intent=null error=Worker VM stopped; next tick: state=paused previous_state=failed; terminal? false; result available? no; vm retained? true; 5 more ticks: state=paused, never terminal, VM still held.
recommendation: Add intent: null to the transition fields at lines 800-804 so a terminal outcome always consumes the pending intent, and have runControl re-read state after exclusive() returns instead of reporting a value the next tick invalidates. The cancel/destroy variants of the same race are benign because the stale intent equals the operator's requested outcome; only 'pause' converts a terminal failure into a non-terminal state.

title: A follow-up acknowledged as queued is never delivered and wedges the worker permanently after pause of an ambiguous-delivery worker
evidence: queueMessage() handles a paused worker whose previous_state is terminal (lines 226-237) by only patching previous_state to 'booting' and enqueueing the new run; it never cancels the predecessor run. The cancelDispatches(id) that would do so is gated on w.state being 'failed'/'recovery_required' (lines 220-224), and here w.state is 'paused'. The ambiguous-delivery path that creates this situation, monitor() at lines 568-579, moves the worker to recovery_required without calling cancelDispatches, so the run stays 'sending'. store.dispatch() (src/store.ts:236-240) returns the OLDEST non-terminal run, so step()'s ready branch (src/coordinator.ts:475-484) selects the stale 'sending' run instead of the newly queued 'pending' one, takes the monitor path, and re-escalates to recovery_required on the next tick. Because recovery_required is terminal (src/domain.ts:14-19), runTick filters the worker out (lines 344-349) and runRecover returns early (line 420), so nothing can ever clear it.
reproduction: Local fakes only, Bun 1.4.2, /tmp/probe/tests/rev-dispatch-finding.test.ts (log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/dispatch-probe.log, exit 1, 1 fail/1 pass). Steps: run worker to 'running'; set the run to state 'sending' with sent_at aged 120s and an empty idle snapshot (the exact shape claimDispatch commits before a crash); tick -> recovery_required; control(pause) -> paused with previous_state 'recovery_required'; message() returns {delivery:'queued', state:'paused'}; control(resume); 30 further ticks. Observed: 'after 30 ticks -> recovery_required | submits: 1 | runs: sending,pending' and the acknowledged follow-up run remains 'pending'. The control case in the same file, identical but without the pause, cancels the stale run and reaches 'submits: 2'. A second triage probe showed a second follow-up is also accepted and also never delivered; an explicit cancel clears both.
recommendation: In the w.state === 'paused' && terminal.has(w.previous_state) branch, call store.cancelDispatches(id) before enqueue() whenever previous_state is terminal and not 'cancelled' (the predecessor turn is over, so any still-open run is undeliverable and only store.dispatch() can reselect it). Alternatively refuse or report recovery_required instead of returning delivery 'queued' when store.dispatch(id) is not the run just enqueued. Apply the same treatment to the quiesce recovery_required path at lines 919-926, which also reaches a terminal state with open runs. A throwaway fix-candidate test in /tmp confirmed the cancelDispatches variant makes the follow-up submit.

title: send_worker_message has no idempotency key, so a client retry enqueues the same instruction as a second turn
evidence: Coordinator.message()/queueMessage() (lines 192-250) unconditionally inserts a new run via Store.enqueue (src/store.ts:213-228), which mints a fresh run_id and message_id. The MCP tool schema is only { worker_id, message } (src/mcp.ts:120-126). Unlike spawn_worker, which documents request_id-based retry collapsing and enforces a body fingerprint (src/mcp.ts:73, src/store.ts:75-85), no caller-supplied key exists for follow-up messages.
reproduction: Code-evidenced; not separately executed. store.enqueue has no conditional insert, so two identical send_worker_message calls always create two runs, and each is delivered to OpenCode with its own messageID (src/providers/opencode.ts:96).
recommendation: Accept an optional request_id on send_worker_message and collapse retries on it, mirroring Store.create with a UNIQUE(worker_id, request_id) index plus an argument fingerprint check. Flagged so the delivery boundary is explicit: docs/MCP-API.md:29 only prescribes request_id reuse for creation, so this is at-least-once by design rather than a regression.

title: A permanently failing pause/resume leaves a durable intent that blocks every other control operation, disables the deadline and suppresses reconciliation
evidence: runControl refuses any differing intent while one is pending (src/coordinator.ts:828-829) and that check precedes the redundant-pause early return (:832), so pause/cancel/destroy all throw 'Another worker control operation is pending'. applyControl pause/resume call the provider with no absence handling (:848 pauseWorker, :859 resumeWorker) unlike cancel (:882-889 vmMissing) and destroy (:913 getWorker). step's catch (:510-517) only patches error, so the intent stays durable. step handles the intent before the deadline check (:440-443 vs :452-455). recover returns early for intent-bearing workers (:407), so the confirmed-absence path (:408-419) never records vm_missing or frees capacity. queueMessage refuses messages only for cancel/destroy intents (:201-208). Reproduced with local fakes (/tmp/probes/probe4.test.ts): variant 1 (pause permanently failing, guest alive) -> 'state: running intent: pause ... expired deadline ignored: true', cancel and destroy both throw, guest still running; variant 2 (paused, guest deleted out of band, resume) -> 'after ticks: paused intent: resume vm_missing: false', message acknowledged 'delivery: queued' with dispatches 'sent,pending', force destroy throws.
reproduction: cd /tmp/probes && /tmp/bun142/bin/bun test probe4.test.ts (Bun 1.4.2, exit 0, 2 pass)
recommendation: In applyControl pause/resume, catch the provider error and probe the existing vmMissing(w.vm_id); on confirmed absence settle immediately (pause -> previous_state, resume -> previous_state ?? 'ready') with vm_missing true and intent cleared. In runControl let cancel/destroy supersede a pending pause/resume intent. Do not let the w.intent early return in recover skip the absence check for pause/resume intents.

title: pause_worker escapes terminal states and lets reconciliation overwrite the reason a worker settled
evidence: The MCP pause tool (src/mcp.ts:127-140) applies no state gate, and runControl (:816-836) only rejects destroyed/vm_missing/differing intent/non-paused resume/redundant pause, so applyControl pause transitions completed, failed, cancelled and recovery_required workers to the non-terminal 'paused' with previous_state set to the terminal state (:851-855). recover skips only terminal.has(w.state) (:420), so a VM reporting 'stopped' moves the record to recovery_required with error 'VM stopped; inspect before resuming' (:429-432); resume_worker is then refused ('Worker is not paused'). Reproduced (/tmp/probes/probe1.test.ts, probe3.test.ts): 'completed after pause: paused previous_state: completed'; 'failed error: test suite red: 3 failures' -> 'after reconcile: recovery_required error: VM stopped; inspect before resuming previous_state: failed' -> resume THREW 'Worker is not paused'; the original summary survives only in store.result. src/cli/overview.ts:277-283 gates pause to ready/running/waiting, showing the transition is unintended; no lifecycle test pauses a settled worker.
reproduction: cd /tmp/probes && /tmp/bun142/bin/bun test probe1.test.ts (Bun 1.4.2, exit 0, 2 pass); probe3.test.ts reproduces the error clobber before erroring on my own later resume call
recommendation: Reject pause when terminal.has(w.state), keeping cancel/destroy; or keep the terminal state authoritative by having recover() also skip records whose previous_state is terminal and never overwrite error for an already-settled worker.

title: cancel settles as cancelled when quiescence could not be proven, unlike fail and destroy
evidence: quiesce returns 'paused' both for a genuinely paused guest and for the ambiguous case where the OpenCode stop failed, pauseWorker failed and the guest still exists (:739-744). fail maps that to recovery_required (:785-798) and destroy to recovery_required (:918-926), but the cancel path only inspects for 'missing' (:890) and otherwise transitions to cancelled with no error. Code-evidenced; not separately reproduced.
reproduction: Reuse the fake setup of tests/lifecycle.test.ts:505 (exec 'systemctl stop' returning code 1 plus pauseWorker throwing) with intent=cancel instead of an expired deadline.
recommendation: Treat quiesce() === 'paused' as recovery_required in the cancel path, as fail() already does, so an unproven stop is visible and the retained guest is not silently reported as cancelled.

title: Control intent recorded during an in-flight step is applied after that step settles the worker, regressing a terminal state to paused
evidence: runControl (src/coordinator.ts:833-834) stores the intent durably then calls exclusive(id, step); exclusive (:251-257) returns the in-flight step promise, so the control never runs its own step. store.finish (src/store.ts:291) and the settled fail transition (src/coordinator.ts:800-804) leave w.intent set, and runTick (:345) admits any worker with an intent regardless of state, so applyControl (:837-856) pauses an already-terminal worker. Reproduced: state regressed completed -> paused with previous_state 'completed' (events worker.completed -> worker.paused) and recovery_required -> paused with previous_state 'recovery_required'.
reproduction: tests/helpers.ts doubles only. /tmp/rev-scope/probe/pause-race.test.ts PROBE 1: run to running, agent.complete, gate agent.inspect mid-monitor(), call control(id,'pause') while the step holds the lock, release. Output: after completion {state:completed,intent:pause}, after one tick {state:paused,previous_state:completed}; a follow-up message is answered {state:paused,delivery:queued} and stays dispatch state 'pending' with submitted still 1 after two more ticks. PROBE 2: same race with no reply, so the in-flight monitor fails the worker as ambiguous delivery -> {state:recovery_required,intent:pause} then {state:paused,previous_state:recovery_required}. Real window: agent.inspect (2 guest calls, 30s bound each) and pushBranch (120s bound).
recommendation: Do not let an intent survive a terminal transition: re-validate in step before applyControl (only cancel/destroy should act on terminal states) and clear intent in store.finish and in fail's settled transitions, so a stale intent cannot regress completed/recovery_required to paused. Report the resulting state to the caller instead of silently regressing.

title: Follow-up queued while a paused worker holds a terminal previous_state inflates the post-resume provisioning window by up to the pause duration
evidence: queueMessage stamps provision_started_at: Date.now() (src/coordinator.ts:235) while the worker is paused, and applyControl resume then adds elapsed = Date.now() - paused_at to that stamp (:863-865), double counting the already-elapsed part of the pause. The boot guard at src/coordinator.ts:444-451 (SWARMFORGE_PROVISION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300) therefore cannot fire for that duration.
reproduction: /tmp/rev-scope/probe/provision-window.test.ts PROBE 3: complete the worker, pause it, set paused_at 1h in the past, send a follow-up, resume. Output: after message {state:paused,previous_state:ready,provision_started_at_in:0}; after resume {state:ready,provision_started_at_in_s:3600,boot_window_remaining_s:3900} instead of the configured 300s.
recommendation: Do not overwrite provision_started_at with Date.now() in queueMessage while paused, or clamp the resume shift to the time actually elapsed since the stamp, so the configured provision window is not silently extended.

title: cancel reports 'cancelled' when the guest could not be proven stopped, and never retries quiescing
evidence: applyControl('cancel') consumes only quiesce() === 'missing' (line 890) and then transitions to 'cancelled' with error:null (line 895). quiesce() returns 'paused' - contract comment at lines 720-724: guest alive, not provably stopped - when systemctl stop is not code 0 (731-737), when pauseWorker throws (739-743), or when the confirmation probe is ambiguous (744). Sibling paths escalate the same outcome: fail() -> recovery_required (785-804) and destroy -> recovery_required (917-926). runTick skips terminal states without intent (340-353) and runRecover only reacts to provider states paused/pausing/stopped (421-432), so a running guest is never re-checked. docs/MCP-API.md:13 documents cancel as 'Stops execution'.
reproduction: Reproduced with repo fakes (/tmp/probe/tests/probe-cancel.test.ts probe A, bun 1.4.2): run to running, make provider.exec answer {code:1} for 'systemctl stop' and pauseWorker throw, then control(id,'cancel') -> state cancelled, error null, VM still present in state 'running'; after 5 more ticks plus recover(): zero further systemctl stop attempts, state still cancelled. Probe B: identical faults with destroy -> recovery_required. Real provider (src/providers/freestyle.ts:279-301, 88-95) throws on any non-2xx from pause/exec, so a single transient Freestyle outage during cancel reaches the 'paused' fallback.
recommendation: Mirror the sibling escalation in the cancel branch: if quiesce() returns 'paused', transition to recovery_required with an explicit 'OpenCode could not be stopped; inspect' error (retryable intent) or keep cancelled but set a non-null error flagging an un-quiesced guest; never clear intent on an unproven stop.

title: Failed control-intent application falls through to fallback completion, reporting 'completed' and blocking cancel/destroy
evidence: step()'s catch (510-526) special-cases GitHandoffError (518) but not control-intent failures. When applyControl('pause') (839-857) throws while the worker is running/waiting, the catch reads .swarmforge/result.json via fallback() (673-691) and promotes it through complete() (692-719), pushing the branch, while the intent stays recorded. runControl then refuses every other intent (828-829).
reproduction: Reproduced (probe H): run to running, seed the active run's .swarmforge/result.json, make pauseWorker throw, then control(id,'pause') -> 'completed intent:pause error:null' though nothing was paused; cancel -> refused 'Another worker control operation is pending'; destroy -> refused; after 3 ticks state completed with intent pause and error 'Provider or OpenCode operation failed; retrying within deadline'.
recommendation: In step()'s catch, re-read the worker and return early after the error patch when w.intent is set, so the intent is retried next pass instead of completing the turn; also ensure complete()/finish() does not report success while an intent is pending.

title: Acknowledged-then-dropped send_worker_message outside the tearingDown hold
evidence: The VM-disappeared branches call store.cancelDispatches without a teardown hold (lines 411 and 489); queueMessage refuses only while tearingDown has the id or intent is set (196-208). During the awaited provider.getWorker() the worker still reads running and vm_missing:false, so a message is acknowledged delivery:'queued' and then silently marked cancelled by that branch.
reproduction: Reproduced (probe G): gate getWorker, delete the VM from the fake provider, call message(id,'racing message') while gated -> queued with state running; after release the worker is failed/vm_missing and the acked run is cancelled. Impact is bounded because the workspace is already lost; it violates the invariant asserted at lines 197-200.
recommendation: Wrap the cancelDispatches calls at lines 411 and 489 in this.teardown(...) (as fail() does) or take the hold before the getWorker await, so the refusal window matches the documented linearization.

title: Persistence probe always reports unsafe when SWARMFORGE_GIT_TREE is an absolute local path, permanently blocking non-forced destroy and routing failures to recovery_required
evidence: The scan roots include SWARMFORGE_GIT_TREE whenever it startsWith('/') (src/safety.ts:14), so the configured source tree is walked as if it were worker output. For a bare repository, `git -C root rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails (src/safety.ts:28) so os.walk runs and the first directory's files trigger `files outside a Git repository` (src/safety.ts:35). A non-bare local path also fails, via `commits not represented by remote refs` (src/safety.ts:41). Absolute local paths are a documented option (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:79 'Clone URL, local path, or none[:tree]'; docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:15). Local probe with a real bare tree and a clean, fully mirrored workspace: GIT_TREE=<abs bare path> -> {safe:false, reason:'files outside a Git repository'}; GIT_TREE=<ssh URL> -> {safe:true}; GIT_TREE=<abs work tree> -> {safe:false, reason:'commits not represented by remote refs'}.
reproduction: /tmp/opencode/rev06/probes/safety-bare.ts (exit 0): seeds a git repo, bare-clones it to an absolute path, clones it into a workspace root, commits, sets refs/remotes/origin/<branch> as pushBranch does; `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is empty and `git rev-list --count --branches HEAD --not --remotes` is 0, yet inspectPersistence returns safe:false for the absolute tree forms.
recommendation: Scan only roots the worker owns (SWARMFORGE_WORKSPACE and result.git.workspace). Treat the configured tree as read-only input, or detect a non-work-tree root (`git -C root rev-parse --is-bare-repository`) and skip it, instead of walking it as worker output.
confidence: high - reproduced locally with real git; coordinator consequence is code-evident (src/coordinator.ts:952 refuses destroy; src/coordinator.ts:802 routes fail() to recovery_required). Existing tests never exercise it: tests/safety.test.ts uses SWARMFORGE_GIT_TREE 'opaque-tree' with a single workspace root, and tests/lifecycle.test.ts fakes the verdict via FakeProvider.dirty.

title: A persistence probe that exceeds SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS leaves destroy permanently pending instead of refusing into recovery_required
evidence: The destroy path awaits `this.bounded(inspectPersistence(...))` with no catch (src/coordinator.ts:944-951). bounded() rejects on the outer promise, so inspectPersistence's internal catch (src/safety.ts:48) never converts it to safe:false; step() swallows the error (src/coordinator.ts:510-518) and leaves intent:'destroy' durable, retried every poll tick (src/coordinator.ts:340-353) with no backoff. The identical call on the failure path does catch it and produces recovery_required (src/coordinator.ts:788-798). The reported error 'Provider or OpenCode operation failed; retrying within deadline' is also inaccurate because step() returns on a pending intent before the deadline check (src/coordinator.ts:440-443). The Git script itself can exceed the bound: several subprocess.run(timeout=15) Git calls per root (src/safety.ts:22-41) against a default 30000ms API bound (src/config.ts:89).
reproduction: /tmp/opencode/rev06/probes/destroy-timeout.ts (exit 0) with FakeProvider and SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS=40 whose GIT_CHECK exec never settles: control(id,'destroy') resolved without throwing; after 3 ticks state='running', intent='destroy', error='Provider or OpenCode operation failed; retrying within deadline', VM still present. Same timeout via the deadline path: state='recovery_required', intent=null.
recommendation: Mirror the fail() handling: catch the bounded rejection and store.transition(id,'recovery_required',{intent:null, deadline_at:null, error:'Persistence check timed out'}) so an unverifiable probe refuses instead of looping.
confidence: high - reproduced with the fake provider; the trigger (large or slow workspace) is inferred from the script's own 15s-per-command bound. tests/lifecycle.test.ts:135 covers a failing destroyWorker only, and no test asserts that destroy settles into recovery_required when the probe is unavailable.

title: Forced destruction leaves no API-visible or durable trace that persistence checks were skipped
evidence: force_destroy is persisted on the worker record (src/coordinator.ts:833) and consulted at src/coordinator.ts:912, but publicWorker (src/security.ts:126-157) exposes only pending_control (line 144) and never force_destroy; the destroyed transition passes no marker (src/coordinator.ts:969-974) and store.transition emits worker.destroyed with empty event data (src/store.ts:166). The CLI always sends force:false (src/cli/client.ts:119), so the case is reachable through the MCP destroy_worker tool (src/mcp.ts:144-146).
reproduction: Code trace only: grep of src/ shows force_destroy written and read only inside coordinator.ts/domain.ts; no reader in publicWorker, list_workers or get_worker_logs.
recommendation: Expose force_destroy from publicWorker and include it in the worker.destroyed event data so an incident reviewer can distinguish a verified destroy from an authorized loss.
confidence: high - code-evidenced, not probe-verified; no test asserts forced-destroy observability.

title: recovery_required is terminal and unresumable even when the coordinator parked the worker on a paused/stopped guest, and the emitted error tells the operator to resume
evidence: runControl accepts resume only when w.state === 'paused' (:830-831, throws 'Worker is not paused'); recovery_required is in terminal (src/domain.ts:17-23); runRecover returns for terminal states at :420 before the paused/stopped mapping at :421-432, making the !terminal.has guard at :429 dead code; runTick filters terminal states out at :344-349. Entry points reproduced: interrupted submit -> recovery_required 'Prompt delivery ambiguous' on a running idle guest (:561-579, :575); stopped guest -> recovery_required 'VM stopped; inspect before resuming' (:429-432); quiesce that could only pause the guest -> recovery_required (:785-804, :909-926). applyControl can already resume a paused guest (:915-916) and holds resumeWorker (:859), both unreachable for these workers. The retained VM keeps consuming SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS capacity (:317-322).
reproduction: Disposable lab /tmp/opencode/rev07/lab with Bun 1.4.2 and tests/helpers FakeProvider/FakeAgent. probes/p1.test.ts P1: worker to running, guest state 'stopped', recover() -> recovery_required, control(id,'resume') -> 'Worker is not paused', second restart + recover + tick unchanged. probes/p1.test.ts P2: agent.abort throws and exec fails for 'systemctl stop' -> recovery_required with guest 'paused'; resume refused again after restart. probes/p2.test.ts P5: dispatch left 'sending' with an idle session and no message -> first tick recovery_required with guest 'running'; resume refused. probes/p3.test.ts P8: send_worker_message does recover it (recovery_required -> booting -> running) but cancels the original dispatch, runs = ['cancelled:Implement a feature','sent:please continue'], so the spawned prompt is never re-delivered. probes/p2.test.ts P4: with SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS=2, two retained-VM workers keep a third spawn 'queued' and provider.created stays 2.
recommendation: Make the recovery path match the emitted messages: handle a paused/stopped guest for a terminal recovery_required worker before the terminal return in runRecover (transition to paused with previous_state), or accept resume when state is recovery_required and the guest is paused/stopped (resumeWorker then transition to previous_state ?? 'ready'). Otherwise reword both errors to 'destroy or send a follow-up' and surface the stranded dispatch's message text so the prompt is recoverable.

title: result.json fallback requires the optional run_id, so a schema-valid file result is discarded when the session is unreadable
evidence: fallback() returns null unless r.run_id === d.run_id (:685), while resultSchema marks run_id optional (src/domain.ts:45) and identify() overwrites run_id with the dispatch's run id anyway (:665-672), so the check is only a staleness guard applied inconsistently with the message path (:589-593).
reproduction: probes/p3.test.ts P7: settled session with no reply plus a result file without run_id -> worker 'waiting', store.result() null; the same file with run_id -> 'completed'.
recommendation: Treat a missing run_id as matching when it is the only unresolved dispatch for that worker, or record the dispatch run id in the artifact the bootstrap already writes; at minimum report the discarded result in the worker error so a successful report is not silently lost.

title: A durable-but-unappliable control intent permanently disables the task deadline and token-idle quiescence and cannot be cleared
evidence: step() returns from `if (w.intent) { await this.applyControl(w); return; }` before the deadline check (line 452) and before monitor()/the token-idle budget (lines 612-626). runControl persists `intent` at line 833; when applyControl throws, step's catch (lines 510-526) only patches `error` and never clears the intent. runRecover skips workers with a pending intent (line 407), and a different intent is refused at lines 828-829, so cancel/destroy cannot clear it and no restart can. control() resolves successfully because step swallows the error, so pause_worker/resume_worker answer as applied while get_worker still shows state running with pending_control (src/security.ts:144).
reproduction: Reproduced with local fakes in /tmp/rev08/probe/deadline-intent.test.ts (6/6 probes pass). pauseWorker always throws; control(id,'pause') resolves with state 'running' and intent 'pause'; after setting deadline_at and token_progress_at to 10x the idle budget in the past, 5 further ticks leave state 'running', intent 'pause', no `systemctl stop`, resume/cancel/destroy all refused ('Another worker control operation is pending'), and a queued message is never submitted. Control test with no intent pending shows the deadline path does fire (state failed, stop issued). A second probe shows the same for a stuck resume intent on a paused worker (deadline stays expired and unenforced); a third shows a completed run flipped to paused/previous_state completed by the leftover intent.
recommendation: Clear or escalate the intent when applyControl throws (record intent_since and move to recovery_required with the provider error after N attempts), evaluate the deadline and idle budget before the intent branch for non-teardown intents, and have control() report the unapplied intent instead of resolving.

title: A turn that already settled is discarded as 'Worker task timed out' instead of completed
evidence: The deadline check (lines 452-455) runs before the running/waiting branch reaches monitor() (lines 486-509), which is the only path that settles a turn and collects the result (structured reply or run_id-matched result.json at lines 588-609 and 673-691). The token-idle budget deliberately does the opposite and is documented to apply only to an active dispatch without a result (lines 610-611). claimDispatch starts the deadline at claim (src/store.ts:251-264), so delivery and Git time also consume the budget.
reproduction: Reproduced in /tmp/rev08/probe/deadline-settle.test.ts: run to running, agent.complete(), then deadline_at = Date.now()-1; one tick yields state failed/recovery_required with error 'Worker task timed out', store.result() null and the dispatch cancelled. The control probe (unexpired deadline, identical snapshot) yields state completed with the result.
recommendation: Let monitor() run before enforcing the deadline, or gate the deadline on the dispatch being unsettled, so a settled turn with a valid result completes and only an unsettled one is quiesced (matching docs/ENVIRONMENT.md).

title: Deadline and idle enforcement latency is serialized behind the periodic reconcile
evidence: runTick awaits this.recover() (lines 308-315) before the per-worker step fan-out (lines 340-353). runRecover awaits listWorkers() and one getWorker() per worker, each bounded by SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30s), so a degraded provider API blocks every deadline check, token-idle quiesce and dispatch delivery for roughly two API timeouts, while the `ticking` guard skips the intervening polls.
reproduction: Not reproduced: the reconcile only runs 30s after the previous one, so a deterministic probe needs a 30s wait. The ordering is code-evident (await at line 311 precedes the step fan-out).
recommendation: Run the reconcile concurrently with or after the step fan-out and bound it below SWARMFORGE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS so it cannot starve deadline enforcement.

title: A schema-valid result is discarded at completion when Git push metadata is merged, and the push is then retried every tick
evidence: Ingest validates the agent payload with resultSchema.safeParse (line 589) or resultSchema.parse in fallback (line 684), but complete() re-validates at line 707 AFTER merging git metadata at line 703 (branch/commit/base_commit/review_url/persisted/dirty, measured +181 bytes) and after Redactor.value, which can also grow strings (a short-userinfo URL https://<redacted>@host becomes https://[REDACTED]@host, +7 bytes; src/security.ts:8-31). The 60 KiB refine at src/domain.ts:71-73 is therefore applied to a different, larger value than the one accepted, so any result in roughly the 61259-61440 byte band throws 'Structured result exceeds 60 KiB; place large reports in artifacts'. store.finish (line 708) and the guest mirror (lines 710-718) never run, so the run is never recorded. The catch block at lines 510-525 only short-circuits for GitHandoffError (line 518), so a ZodError re-enters fallback()->complete()->pushBranch on every poll tick.
reproduction: Local fakes only, probes at /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe2.test.ts and probe5.test.ts (Bun 1.4.2, in-memory SQLite). A 61178-byte resultSchema-valid payload: push=github-app -> state=running, err=[{message:'Structured result exceeds 60 KiB; place large reports in artifacts'}]; identical payload with SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_MODE=none -> state=completed, err=none. With a 1s deadline and 1.6s of ticking: pushBranch calls = 1343, final state = failed, error = 'Worker task timed out', store.result() = null, no result.received event, guest result.json mirror never written. Tracked 61 bytes of headroom vs the 181-byte git addition.
recommendation: Do not make a post-merge re-parse fatal. Either validate once on the value that will be stored (validate before line 703 and merge git after), or clamp/trim and record a distinct warning when the merged result exceeds 61440 bytes instead of throwing. Additionally add a GitHandoffError-style early return (or a one-shot attempt latch) around any post-push failure so the catch block cannot re-push every tick.
confidence: high - reproduced deterministically; only the payload size band is narrow (0.3% of the cap)

title: The 60 KiB result cap is enforced but never disclosed to the producer, and its rejection is unattributable
evidence: resultSchema.toJSONSchema() (1,462 bytes as emitted at src/providers/opencode.ts:51) contains maxLength for every field but no trace of the .refine; probed: 'mentions 60 KiB: false', because refinements are not representable in JSON Schema. The advertised bounds sum to about 330 KB (summary 4000 + details 16000 + files_changed 200x1024 + warnings 50x2000 + followup_reason 4000), while the enforced total is 61440 bytes. An over-cap result is rejected at ingest and the worker is failed with the generic text 'Missing or malformed structured result' (src/coordinator.ts:597-600); no size hint reaches the model, the worker record, or the operator, even though docs/WORKER-PROTOCOL.md:27 states the 60 KiB cap.
reproduction: Probes /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe4.test.ts (emitted schema inspection) and /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe6.test.ts: a per-field-valid 200657-byte result gives schema ok = false and 'state = failed | error = Missing or malformed structured result'.
recommendation: State the total-size cap in the bootstrap() text beside the schema and/or add a description to the emitted JSON Schema, and include the resultSchema issue path (size exceeded) in the failure text so the producer can self-correct and the operator can triage. This also removes most of F1's exposure by keeping generated results well below the band.

title: An assistant message carrying both an error and a parseable structured payload completes the run and drops the error
evidence: reply is selected as the newest completed assistant message with 'm.result !== undefined || m.error' (line 585), then resultSchema.safeParse(reply.result) is attempted before any check of reply.error (lines 589-599). The SDK declares structured?: unknown on the assistant message independently of error (node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/v2/gen/types.gen.d.ts:243), so the combination is representable, and the mapped snapshot preserves both (src/providers/opencode.ts, result: info.structured ?? parseJsonText(text), error: info.error?.name). A parseable payload therefore wins over the error and is stored as a completed run with error = null; the provider/session error is never recorded in the worker record or events.
reproduction: Probe /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe6.test.ts (second test): a completed assistant message given error = 'ProviderOverloadedError' plus a valid structured payload yields 'state = completed | error = null' with the payload stored as the run result.
recommendation: When reply.error is set, take the failure path unless the adopted result came from the current-run result.json fallback, or at minimum log both the session error and the adopted result so the error is not silently dropped.
confidence: medium - coordinator logic reproduced; whether OpenCode 1.18.31 actually populates structured on an errored message is unverified (needs a live server, out of scope)

title: send_worker_message to a paused worker acknowledges a follow-up that is queued behind a stale dispatch and is later silently cancelled
evidence: queueMessage decides whether to discard the worker's dead run with `if (w.state === "failed" || w.state === "recovery_required")` (coordinator.ts:220) and calls cancelDispatches only there. A worker that is `paused` with previous_state `recovery_required` skips that block; the branch at coordinator.ts:226-237 only rewrites previous_state to booting/ready and returns delivery:"queued" (coordinator.ts:244-249). The stale unresolved dispatch exists because the reconciliation paths do not cancel dispatches: coordinator.ts:429-432 (VM stopped -> recovery_required) and coordinator.ts:573-578 (ambiguous delivery). step() at state ready (coordinator.ts:475-484) then selects store.dispatch(id), i.e. the oldest unresolved row (store.ts:236-240, ORDER BY rowid), so the acknowledged run stays pending and when the token-idle watchdog quiesces the blocked run, fail() -> cancelDispatches (coordinator.ts:799) cancels the acknowledged follow-up too.
reproduction: /tmp/opencode/rev10/probes/followup-order.test.ts (repo harness, in-memory SQLite, FakeProvider/FakeAgent, token idle timeout 1s). Setup: run worker to running, set the fake VM state to stopped, coordinator.recover() -> recovery_required with an unresolved `sent` dispatch; then pause_worker, send_worker_message, resume_worker + ticks. Observed: message acknowledged with delivery:"queued"; dispatches = `sent:Implement a feature`, `pending:<new message>`; after resume, submissions after the acknowledged message = 0; final state failed with "No token progress for 1s; worker quiesced" and the acknowledged dispatch state = "cancelled". Control test A (same setup without pause) behaves correctly: head dispatch is the new run and state becomes booting.
recommendation: Key the stale-dispatch cancellation on the effective state, e.g. `const effective = w.state === "paused" ? w.previous_state : w.state;` and apply the existing vm_id/opencode_session_id check plus store.cancelDispatches(id) when `effective` is `failed` or `recovery_required`, before enqueueing. Add a regression test covering pause -> message -> resume on a recovery_required worker that still holds an unresolved dispatch.

title: get_worker_result without run_id can return an earlier run's success as the latest result for a failed current run
evidence: Store.result() filters dispatches to those that already have a result and returns the last one (store.ts:300-306); get_worker_result returns only {worker_id, result} (mcp.ts:150-162), so no worker state or latest dispatch run_id accompanies it. Runs that settle without a structured result (deadline/token-idle quiesce, provider failure, unresolved recovery_required) leave no row, so the payload describes an earlier run.
reproduction: /tmp/opencode/rev10/probes/stale-result.test.ts: run 1 completes with a structured result, follow-up run 2 is queued and then fails via the deadline path; store.get(id).state === 'failed' while store.result(id) returns summary 'run one ok', run_id c1422aa7, status 'completed' (actual latest run fbb50a1c). Reported run_id !== latest run.
recommendation: When run_id is omitted, also return the worker state and the latest dispatch run_id (or an explicit is_latest_run flag) so staleness is checkable from a single response.

title: Stale `error` survives finish()'s re-arm of a failed worker to `ready`
evidence: finish() writes `error: result.summary` on the transition to the terminal result state (src/store.ts:294), then re-arms a worker that still has a queued dispatch with `this.transition(id, "ready", { completed_at: null })` (src/store.ts:296-297). transition() merges supplied fields over the stored worker (src/store.ts:146-152), so the failure summary persists. The sibling re-arm path in queueMessage explicitly passes `error: null` (src/coordinator.ts:239-243), so the two disagree.
reproduction: Local fake provider/agent from tests/helpers (no cloud calls). Worker to running; coordinator.message(follow-up); agent.complete({status:'failed', summary:'lint gate failed'}); await coordinator.tick(). Result: state = "ready", error = "lint gate failed", completed_at = null. publicWorker() returns {state:'ready', error:'lint gate failed'}. See /tmp/rev11/probe/p8.ts and /tmp/rev11/probe/p12.ts (both exit 0).
recommendation: Clear terminal-only fields on re-arm: `this.transition(id, "ready", { completed_at: null, error: null })`, or normalise error/deadline_at inside transition() whenever the target state is non-terminal.
confidence: high - reproduced end-to-end; consumers are display-only (src/security.ts:146, src/cli/overview.ts:232, src/runtime.ts:94), so impact is observability rather than state-machine corruption

title: cancelDispatches() is the only multi-row mutation in store.ts with no transaction, and is never paired atomically with the terminal transition
evidence: cancelDispatches() (src/store.ts:246-250) loops dispatches calling saveDispatch(), each an independent implicit commit. Every other multi-statement invariant wraps this.db.transaction(...): create (:71), transition (:158), claimDispatch (:252), finish (:278). Coordinator always calls cancelDispatches() then a separate transition() (src/coordinator.ts:411-418, :489-495, :775-783, :799-804, :894-905, :935-958, :968-975), so 'all dispatches cancelled AND worker terminal' is never a single commit. The two statements are synchronous with no await between them, so there is no JS interleaving window; a crash window requires killing the process mid-window.
reproduction: Injected a throw on the 2nd saveDispatch inside cancelDispatches: resulting dispatch states were ["cancelled", "pending", "pending"] (partial cancellation). See /tmp/rev11/probe/p7.ts (exit 0). Crash-window impact traced by code: a worker left in running/waiting with all dispatches cancelled falls through monitor() to transition 'waiting' (src/coordinator.ts:536-539) until deadline_at (set at src/store.ts:256) trips the timeout check at src/coordinator.ts:452-455.
recommendation: Wrap the loop in this.db.transaction(...)(). Stronger: add one store method that cancels dispatches and applies the terminal transition in a single transaction, and replace every cancelDispatches()+transition() pair in the coordinator with it.
confidence: high for the atomicity gap (reproduced); medium for real-world impact, which is bounded by the single-writer process lock (src/runtime.ts:145) and busy_timeout=5000 (src/store.ts:22)

title: request_id retry idempotency depends on the config-resolved SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
evidence: create() fingerprints the resolved input: `createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify(input))` (src/store.ts:72-74). input is built by Coordinator.spawn, which fills timeout_seconds from config.SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS when the caller omits it (src/coordinator.ts:185-190). src/store.ts:81-82 then throws "request_id already used with different arguments" on mismatch, so an operator setting is baked into the idempotency key.
reproduction: Two Coordinator instances over one Store differing only in SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (3600 -> 1800), same request_id and identical body: retry rejected with 'request_id already used with different arguments'. See /tmp/rev11/probe/p11.ts (exit 0).
recommendation: Fingerprint only caller-supplied arguments (hash the spawnSchema output before timeout_seconds is resolved) and treat the effective timeout as mutable metadata, or compare a canonicalised subset (team/task/role/prompt) and log rather than reject a timeout-only difference.
confidence: high - reproduced; not covered by tests/lifecycle.test.ts:13-17 or tests/core.test.ts:88-120, which retry under unchanged config with an explicit timeout_seconds. Breaks the documented 'use request_id for safe retries' contract (src/mcp.ts:73, ARCHITECTURE.md)

title: /metrics render is O(retained workers x retained events); one scrape blocks the single-threaded control plane
evidence: render() iterates store.all() (:74) and per worker issues store.tokens({worker_id}) (:84), 'GROUP BY type WHERE worker_id=?' (:100-104), 'min(at) ... type=worker.ready' (:110-115) and one json_extract(data,'$.run_id') event scan per dispatch (:121-127). events has no index on worker_id, so EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN returns 'SCAN events' for each (src/store.ts:27 defines no such index).
reproduction: Local sqlite3 3.45.1 running metrics.ts's own SQL text: 200 workers/8000 events = 0.525s of SQLite time for one render's statement set; 800 workers/80000 events = 27.55s (10x rows -> ~52x time). Through the real Store at 5000 workers/250k events/100k usage rows a single worker's metrics queries cost 150.8ms, extrapolating to minutes per scrape. Probe scripts probe3.ts and /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/rev12-probes.log; probes live only in /tmp/rev12/probe.
recommendation: Add idempotent indexes events(worker_id, id) and events(worker_id, type, at); replace per-worker event queries with set-based GROUP BY aggregates or persisted running counters; restrict histogram loops to workers with live dispatch history; consider a snapshot updated by the coordinator tick rather than per-scrape recomputation.

title: Store.tokens() full-scans usage due to the '? IS NULL OR col=?' idiom, on the 2s poll path for every active worker
evidence: tokens() filters with 'WHERE (? IS NULL OR worker_id=?) AND (? IS NULL OR team_id=?) AND (? IS NULL OR task_id=?)', which hides the predicate from the planner: plan is 'SCAN usage' + 'SEARCH workers', whereas the identical aggregate with 'WHERE worker_id=?' uses 'SEARCH usage USING sqlite_autoindex_usage_1 (worker_id=?)'. Called from src/coordinator.ts:614-616 on every poll (default SWARMFORGE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=2000, SWARMFORGE_TOKEN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300 so enabled by default), from src/store.ts:261 claimDispatch, src/security.ts:145 publicWorker and src/metrics.ts:84.
reproduction: Real Store.tokens at 5000 workers / 250k events / 100k usage rows: as implemented 7.9ms for one worker; same aggregate with a plain predicate 0.1ms (~80x). With 50 running workers that is ~0.4s of blocking CPU per 2s tick and it grows with total messages ever recorded. probe6.ts in /workspace/.swarmforge/logs.
recommendation: Use two static prepared statements (unfiltered / filtered) or assemble the WHERE fragment from the supplied filters so worker_id=? becomes an index seek; keep the usage primary key.

title: Worker-filtered event pagination has no supporting index and degrades to a full-table scan
evidence: events() uses 'WHERE (? IS NULL OR worker_id=?) AND id>? ORDER BY id LIMIT ?' on a table with no index on worker_id, so the plan is only 'SEARCH events USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid>?)' and every later row is filtered; lifecycleEvents() (:191-212) has the same shape for wait_for_state_change. Reached by get_worker_logs (src/mcp.ts:172-182, after defaults to 0).
reproduction: Real Store on 5000 workers / 250k events: events(mid-table worker, 0, 100) = 20.4ms vs 0.1ms unfiltered; lifecycleEvents(0,{worker_id},200) = 18.8ms. After adding CREATE INDEX ev_worker ON events(worker_id, id) the plan became 'SEARCH events USING INDEX ev_worker (worker_id=? AND id>?)' and the page dropped to 0.2ms (45-135x); the OR-guarded form still chose the rowid seek, so index plus predicate rewrite are both required.
recommendation: Add events(worker_id, id) and events(worker_id, type, at) in the constructor DDL and replace the nullable-parameter OR filters with explicit filtered/unfiltered statements.

title: No retention anywhere: history grows forever and every read path is O(history)
evidence: No DELETE, prune, VACUUM or retention setting exists anywhere in src (grep). destroy_worker only transitions to 'destroyed' (src/coordinator.ts:969); events, dispatches (results up to 60 KiB per domain.ts:44-79), usage rows and worker bodies are kept forever. Readers pay for it: coordinator.ts:316 and :363 call store.all() twice per tick and twice per reconcile; security.ts:48 builds the redactor secret list from store.all() and src/mcp.ts:40 then runs 3 replaceAll variants per retained worker password on every response; mcp.ts:96-113 list_workers scans all workers and slices in JS so limit reduces no work.
reproduction: Real Store at 5000 retained workers: store.all() 5.9ms (twice per 2s tick); redactorFor().value() on a 2KB/20KB payload 13.2ms/15.9ms per response, linear in retained worker count. probe2.ts/probe4.ts.
recommendation: Add an idempotent retention pass (startup + reconcile branch of runTick) pruning events/usage/dispatches for destroyed or cancelled workers past a configurable window, plus periodic wal_checkpoint; push team/task/state filtering into SQL for list_workers/get_task/get_team_status; build the redactor secret set once per request from a targeted query.

title: Completed-dispatch history per worker is unbounded and fully re-parsed on every poll and every tool response
evidence: dispatches() selects every dispatch body for a worker; dispatch() (:236-240) and result() (:300-306) build on it. Only non-terminal dispatches are capped at 100 (src/coordinator.ts:215-217), so completed dispatches with up to 60 KiB results accumulate for a worker reused via send_worker_message. Callers: coordinator.ts:215, :793, :933, :949 and security.ts:146-148 (pending_messages) on every publicWorker.
reproduction: Real Store on a synthetic DB with 20 workers x 300 completed dispatches (78 MB): dispatch(worker) 8.1ms, result(worker) 8.3ms, one publicWorker's store work 8.8ms, and the store work of a list_workers(limit=20) response 95.2ms of synchronous JSON parsing on the event loop. probe5.ts.
recommendation: Query only what callers need: WHERE worker_id=? AND state NOT IN ('completed','cancelled') for the pending-queue check and pending_messages (prefer count(*)), and fetch a result by run_id/latest with a targeted indexed query.

title: workers_state index is never used by any query while every transition maintains it
evidence: All SQL in src writes the workers.state column (store.ts:149) but never filters on it; every state filter is applied in JavaScript after store.all() (mcp.ts:100-106, :263, :277; metrics.ts:75-83; coordinator.ts:172-185, 316-345). The index therefore only adds write cost to the hottest write path.
reproduction: grep of all SQL in src/: the only 'state=' occurrences are the UPDATE statements at store.ts:149 and store.ts:243. Not timing-measured; code-evidenced.
recommendation: Push state filtering into SQL so the index is used (including in list_workers), or drop the index.

title: Event-log cursor is persisted once per event instead of once per flush (fsync amplification)
evidence: eventLogger's loop calls c.store.setting('logged_event', ...) for every event; Store.setting (store.ts:57-63) is its own autocommit transaction, and PRAGMA synchronous is 2 (FULL) on a target-created database (measured with bun:sqlite). Up to 100 such writes per 1000ms flush (serve.ts:193).
reproduction: PRAGMA synchronous = 2 and PRAGMA journal_mode = wal verified on a database created by the target Store (probe1.ts); write count per flush derived from runtime.ts:177-212. No timing benchmark run.
recommendation: Persist 'after' once after the loop completes; the cursor is already restart-safe.

title: No schema-version ledger; positional INSERTs make the first future column addition a runtime break
evidence: The constructor only issues CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and PRAGMA user_version is 0 (measured). 'INSERT INTO workers VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)' (store.ts:118) and 'INSERT INTO dispatches VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)' (store.ts:225) are positional, so a new or reordered column fails at runtime against every retained database instead of being migrated.
reproduction: PRAGMA user_version = 0 verified via probe1.ts. DDL is byte-identical across every commit touching src/store.ts (9ee8fea, 96e556c, 3e54f90, b99de22, d428e0f), so this is latent and not currently triggerable; permanent retention (finding 4) raises the odds over time.
recommendation: Set/check PRAGMA user_version, apply ordered ALTER TABLE migrations in the constructor, and name columns explicitly in the two positional inserts.

title: GET /events re-parses the entire worker table once per string field, stalling the single-threaded event loop
evidence: src/security.ts:43-50 redactorFor() returns a Redactor whose `secrets` is a thunk that calls c.store.all() (SELECT body FROM workers + JSON.parse of every row, each row embedding a prompt of up to 32000 chars per src/domain.ts:33). src/security.ts:7 Redactor.text() invokes this.secrets() on EVERY call, and Redactor.value() recurses into every string field. src/http.ts:45 calls redactor.value(e) for up to 100 events per request, each with 3 string fields (worker_id, type, data) => 300 full table scans + 300 full JSON parses per request. The redactorFor() call at src/http.ts:42 looks like per-request construction but is lazy and snapshots nothing.
reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, local fakes, tmpdir SQLite, no network (probe /tmp/rv13/probe/repro.ts). Production defaults: SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS=50, prompts at the 32000-char schema maximum => 1634620 bytes of worker bodies, 100 events. Result: 'GET /events x3 = 1588ms (529ms per request, single-threaded)'; 'same query WITHOUT the redactor = 0ms'; 'store.all() calls caused by redacting one 100-event page = 300'. Scaling with a full 100-event page: N=25 -> 133ms, N=50 -> 786ms, N=100 -> 2001ms, N=200 -> 4225ms (linear in retained workers x page size). An empty page costs 0-1ms, so cost is entirely per-delivered-event. 6s of reconnect-polling at 50 workers/32000B prompts consumed 5704ms of event loop (951% of one core), because the SSE 'retry: 2000' directive makes a browser EventSource poll this endpoint continuously. Consequence: Bun runs the server on one thread, so this stalls all MCP calls, the coordinator tick (SWARMFORGE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=2000) and /health; SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN is optional (src/config.ts:81).
recommendation: Resolve the secret list once per request instead of per call: in redactorFor, compute the array eagerly and close over the array (or memoize the thunk with a per-request scope). Optionally redact the serialized JSON string once per event rather than walking each field, and add an events(worker_id, id) index (see the companion missing-index note in the MEDIUM finding).
confidence: high - reproduced deterministically; the 300 store.all() calls per 100-event page is an exact count, and the linear scaling was measured across four worker counts

title: wait_for_state_change ignores its own deadline while draining a large event backlog
evidence: next() (src/coordinator.ts:119-135) loops lifecycleEvents(cursor, filter, 200) until it matches or exhausts the table. The deadline is checked only AFTER next() returns, at src/coordinator.ts:141 and :160. With a non-matching `states` filter or a stale cursor, the scan runs to the end of the table regardless of timeout_ms. The events table has no retention (docs/OBSERVABILITY.md:30 makes pruning an operator responsibility) and no index at all (PRAGMA index_list(events) returns []), so the drain grows without bound over server lifetime. metrics.ts:102/113/125 additionally run three unindexed `WHERE worker_id=?` scans plus a temp B-tree group-by per worker per scrape on the same unindexed table.
reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, local fakes (probe /tmp/rv13/probe/drain.ts), single worker, synthetic backlog, call = waitForStateChange({worker_id, cursor:0, states:['destroyed']}, {timeoutMs:0}): 100000 events -> 74ms, 400000 -> 289ms, 1600000 -> 1200ms. timeout_ms=0 is documented as 'checks once' (src/mcp.ts:296, docs/MCP-API.md:23) but performs a full-table drain. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN confirms the scan is a rowid range walk with no worker_id index.
recommendation: Pass the deadline into next() and break out of the batch loop when Date.now() >= deadline, returning the consumed cursor so next_cursor stays accurate. Separately add CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_worker_id ON events(worker_id, id) to fix the same missing-index problem on the metrics surface.
confidence: high for the mechanism and the unbounded-growth property (deterministic, EXPLAIN-confirmed); the 1.6M-event figure is a synthetic upper bound rather than a measured production backlog, so real-world severity depends on how large the operator's events table grows

title: A wait whose synchronous scan races Store.close() rejects with RangeError: Cannot use a closed database instead of 'Server is stopping' or changed:false
evidence: waitForStateChange reads the database before consulting this.stopped: L72 calls this.store.latestEventId() and L139 calls next() (this.store.lifecycleEvents), while the stop check only becomes observable through the `stopping` promise built at L84-L90 and raced at L151. Store.close() (src/store.ts:34-37) clears `watchers`, so a parked waiter is never woken, then closes the handle; the next read throws. The three documented outcomes are Server is stopping (L158), Wait aborted (L157) and changed:false (L91-103); this fourth outcome is not among them.
reproduction: REPRODUCED by direct probe (not reachable in the shipped shutdown order). const p = coordinator.waitForStateChange({worker_id}, {timeoutMs: 300}); await waitForListenerCount(1); store.close(); await p; // => RangeError: Cannot use a closed database. /tmp/opencode/probes/wait-http.test.ts PROBE G2 (exit 0, log printed). Reachability excluded: src/serve.ts:140-157 closes the store at L152 only after await api?.stop(true) and await coordinator?.stop(), which resolves every stopWaiter and yields at await Promise.allSettled(), so parked waiters have unwound first; new MCP requests cannot arrive after api.stop(true).
recommendation: Check this.stopped immediately after the existing pre-abort check at L70 (before the first store read), and make the scan fail soft: treat a closed-database error as result(found ?? null) rather than letting it escape. Optionally have Store.close() resolve parked waiters before clearing `watchers`, since it already holds the listener set.
confidence: medium - reproduced by probe; not reachable through the current serve.ts resource order, so impact today is limited to a non-documented error string

title: list_workers pages can exceed the 128 KiB MCP response cap, making swarmforge status fail entirely
evidence: register() rejects any tool response over 131072 bytes (src/mcp.ts:44). list_workers (src/mcp.ts:101-118) maps every row through publicWorker, which returns the worker error verbatim (src/security.ts:143). Store.finish copies result.summary into error, and resultSchema permits summary up to 4000 chars (src/domain.ts:44). The CLI overview loop hardcodes limit:100 (src/cli/client.ts:77-80) with no error recovery.
reproduction: In-memory MCP server + client. 40 failed workers with 4000-char summaries: list_workers{limit:20} not an error; list_workers{limit:100} returns isError=true with text 'Response exceeds limit; request a smaller page'. Replaying the verbatim cli/client.ts overview loop yields OVERVIEW FAILED. Threshold sweep by worker count at 4000-char summaries: 20 workers = 88,993 bytes (ok), 29 = 129,025 (ok), 30 = 133,473 (exceeds).
recommendation: Bound list_workers payload internally (clip error to a short form for list views, or cap total bytes and return a matching next_offset), and have cli/client.ts catch the oversized-page error and retry with a halved limit rather than propagating the failure.

title: Worker-detail TIMELINE renders the oldest 100 events instead of the newest
evidence: client.inspect calls get_worker_logs with {limit:100} and no cursor (src/cli/client.ts:101-104). Store.events uses 'WHERE id > after ORDER BY id LIMIT ?', so after=0 returns the oldest page (src/store.ts). renderWorkerDetail then renders events.slice(-8) (src/cli/overview.ts:256). Each turn emits several events (worker.running, result.received, worker.ready), so ~30+ follow-up turns exceed 100 events.
reproduction: 40 simulated follow-up turns produce 121 events. The default page ends at event id 100 while the newest event in the log is id 121. With deterministic one-minute event timestamps the rendered TIMELINE ends at 01:40:00 and the true newest event 02:01:00 never appears in the rendered output.
recommendation: Page to the tail in client.inspect (follow the cursor to the final page and keep it), or add a bounded reverse read in Store.events (ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? then reverse) for the detail view.

title: Stale inference map entries permanently inflate get_swarm_status and the Prometheus inference gauge
evidence: Both the reconcile() and step() branches transition a worker to 'paused' on out-of-band VM pause without calling this.inference.delete(worker_id), unlike the control-intent pause path in applyControl which does delete. runTick filters out paused workers, so step()/monitor() never refresh or clear the value. get_swarm_status sums the map (src/mcp.ts:287-290) and metrics.render() sets the gauge from it (src/metrics.ts:80).
reproduction: Harness worker driven to running; snapshot forced to busy with inference_active:1; tick -> estimate 1; provider VM set to paused; tick + recover() + tick -> worker state paused, estimate still 1, map still holds [worker_id, 1].
recommendation: Delete the inference entry in both pause branches, or prune entries for every worker not in an active state at the end of runTick/reconcile so the aggregate is derived from currently polled workers rather than accumulated history.

title: Single-owner process lock is keyed to the configured DB path string, so two aliases of one database file each take their own flock
evidence: src/serve.ts:126 builds the lock as `${config.SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH}.lock` from the raw configured string; src/runtime.ts:150 flocks that path. No canonicalisation exists: host_path is plain text (src/settings/load.ts:376) and SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH is only z.string().min(1) (src/config.ts:77). SQLite, however, resolves the path (it follows a final-component symlink and a hardlink), so two spellings of one file get two lock inodes. The second line of defence is inert: SWARMFORGE_INSTANCE_ID defaults to "default" (src/config.ts:37-39), so the persisted-owner check at src/serve.ts:163-165 compares "default" to "default" and passes. Probe /tmp/opencode/r16/probes/ownership.ts (Bun 1.4.2, exit 0): holding acquireProcessLock(<real>.lock) then calling acquireProcessLock(<symlink alias>.lock) returned ACQUIRED instead of refusing; a Store opened on the alias read the row written through the real path and its write was visible from the real path. A hardlink alias behaved the same. Control: a symlinked *directory* alias correctly REFUSED (one lock inode).
reproduction: Bun 1.4.2 in /tmp: create <dir>/sub/db.sqlite via Store, symlink <dir2>/db.sqlite -> <dir>/sub/db.sqlite, keep unlock1=acquireProcessLock('<dir>/sub/db.sqlite.lock'), then acquireProcessLock('<dir2>/db.sqlite.lock') => ACQUIRED (expected refusal). See logs r16-ownership in /workspace/.swarmforge/logs.
recommendation: Key the lock to the file, not the spelling: canonicalise the parent with realpathSync before deriving the lock path, and/or record the database's dev+ino in the lock file at acquire time and refuse when a live lock names a different inode. Otherwise name the lock path in the refusal message so an alias is visible.
confidence: high on the reproduced lock split; medium on operational likelihood (requires an aliased SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH, and README/ENVIRONMENT.md already require one server process per database), hence LOW not higher

title: Lock refusal message carries no lock path and no holder PID even though the holder PID is durably recorded
evidence: src/runtime.ts:153 throws a bare "Another SwarmForge process owns this database", while src/runtime.ts:160 writes `${process.pid}` into the lock file. No code under src/ reads that file back (grep for lock readers returns nothing), so the recorded PID exists only for an operator to cat by hand. Triggered on every refused start: a healthy owner, a scripts/smoke.ts run, or a process left holding the lock after the forced exit at src/serve-command.ts:120-130.
reproduction: Code trace plus ownership.ts probe: while one process holds the lock, a second acquireProcessLock throws the bare message, and the owner's PID content in the lock file is intact and readable at that moment (before === after, mtime unchanged), i.e. the identifying data is available exactly when the diagnostic is emitted.
recommendation: Include the lock path and the recorded PID in the refusal message, passed through the existing command redactor (src/serve-command.ts:38-53).
confidence: high (code-evidenced, reproduced message and preserved PID); impact limited to operability

title: docs/SERVE.md inverts the listener and log-interval order that src/serve.ts implements (documentation only)
evidence: docs/SERVE.md:40 states the rollback order as "flush and stop the periodic logger, stop the metrics listener, stop the API listener, ...", and docs/SERVE.md:48 says shutdown step 1 is "the readiness gate closes, then the log interval is cleared". src/serve.ts:141-146 does the opposite: clearInterval(logTimer) (141), gate.close() (142), api.stop(true) (143), metricsServer.stop(true) (145). The code order is the safer one (no flush can run after admission closes; the API listener stops before metrics).
reproduction: Line-by-line comparison of docs/SERVE.md:40 and :48 against src/serve.ts:140-157 at the target; no runtime impact.
recommendation: Correct both sentences to match the implementation, or change the code if the documented order is the intended contract.
confidence: high (documentation-only; existing tests assert effects such as existsSync(lock)===false, openDatabaseHandles===0 and port reuse, never the order)

title: A throwing event-log flush escapes the 1s interval and kills the process without the ordered release
evidence: `logTimer = setInterval(flush, 1000)` registers the raw eventLogger callback with no try/catch, while `release()` protects only the one-shot final flush with try/finally (src/serve.ts:148-156). eventLogger (src/runtime.ts:176-212) calls store.events/store.setting plus appendFileSync/renameSync/statSync directly, so it is not tracked by Coordinator's track/idle drain either. Neither serve-command.ts nor main.ts installs an uncaughtException handler, so an interval throw becomes an out-of-band process death: gate not closed, listeners not stopped by SwarmForge, SQLite not closed, lock file not unlinked, final flush skipped, and the raw message never passed through commandRedactor.
reproduction: REPRODUCED. Probe /tmp/rev-17/probes/logflush2.ts: seed one queued worker with the repo's FakeProvider/FakeAgent, mkdir a directory at <db>.log, then startServer. Output: 'started http://127.0.0.1:18897 health 200' then a requested event line then 'UNCAUGHT: Error EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, open /tmp/.../db.sqlite.log', probe exit 42. The server was serving /health 200 immediately before the crash. Control probe /tmp/rev-17/probes/logflush.ts (same unwritable target, no pending events) exited 0, so the fault needs at least one unflushed event. Real triggers are ENOSPC/EACCES/EROFS on the event log or a failed store.setting.
recommendation: Register a guarded callback, e.g. setInterval(() => { try { flush(); } catch (e) { /* redacted report */ } }, 1000). If a persistent fault must be fatal, trigger one bounded ordered shutdown (shutdown() is already idempotent) instead of throwing, so the lock, listeners and database are still released in reverse order and the message is redacted.

title: /health answers 200 for the whole first provisioning pass while every mutation is refused with 503
evidence: The gate stays in 'starting' from the listener bind (src/serve.ts:170-191) until gate.open() (src/serve.ts:203), which happens only after `await withAbort(coordinator.startProvisioning())` at line 194. /health is served by the wrapped handler (src/http.ts:33) and GET is in readOnlyMethods (src/serve.ts:33), so liveness is 200 while POST /mcp is 503 for every tool. The window can reach ~2 minutes by default: the first tick provisions up to SWARMFORGE_MAX_PROVISIONING (4) workers and each provider.createWorker call is bounded by SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS (30s) in coordinator.bounded (src/coordinator.ts:41-59, 457).
reproduction: Code-evidenced and already pinned by the repository's own passing test tests/serve.test.ts:432 ('listeners are reserved before provisioning, refuse mutations until ready'), which asserts { mutation: 503, health: 200 }. No new probe was needed. Impact: a supervisor using /health as its readiness probe marks the instance ready and routes traffic to a process that refuses all mutations.
recommendation: Optionally distinguish readiness from liveness: return 503 with Retry-After on /health while the gate is still starting, add a dedicated /ready that only answers 200 after gate.open(), or move gate.open() before await startProvisioning() so the gated window covers only listener reservation.

title: Shutdown order in the code is the reverse of the documented order
evidence: release() does `clearInterval(logTimer)` (line 141) before `gate.close()` (line 142), while docs/SERVE.md:48 documents 'Stop admission: the readiness gate closes, then the log interval is cleared.'
reproduction: Direct source/doc comparison at target. No functional consequence today: an event produced in the one-statement sliver is still flushed by the final flush at src/serve.ts:149. The risk is that a future change trusts the documented order ('stop admitting first, then stop logging') and inverts the real one.
recommendation: Swap the two statements in release() to match the documented order, or amend docs/SERVE.md:48. Swapping is the safer direction.

title: A second termination signal is swallowed; only the shutdown deadline can end a stuck drain
evidence: onSignal returns immediately when a signal was already recorded (`if (requested) return;`), so repeated SIGINT/SIGTERM cannot escalate a drain that is blocked on a noncancelable provider promise. The process then waits out SWARMFORGE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS (default 60s, serve-command.ts:9) and exits 70.
reproduction: PROBED, behaviour confirmed correct-for-its-documented-design. Probe /tmp/rev-17/probes/signal-matrix.ts spawns the repo's own tests/fixtures/serve-command-child.ts in 'blocked' mode with SWARMFORGE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=400: one SIGTERM -> exit 70 at 650ms; SIGTERM x2 -> exit 70 at 747ms; SIGTERM+SIGINT -> exit 70 at 744ms; all three logged 'Shutdown deadline exceeded; exiting with durable state intact'. The documented contract (docs/SERVE.md:57,65) is met; this is an operational sharp edge, not a correctness bug.
recommendation: Optional: accept a second signal of the other kind, or a third signal, as an immediate process.exit(forcedShutdownExitCode). The deadline path already exits with the database open, so honouring an explicit second request adds no new truncation risk and matches operator expectation.

title: In-flight read-only tool calls raise RangeError: Cannot use a closed database after the drain closes SQLite
evidence: release() closes the store after awaiting only Coordinator-tracked work (src/serve.ts:147). WorkerFiles read-only handlers (src/files.ts:121 store.get after an await on provider.getWorker, src/files.ts:142 store.events) and the lazy redactor secret set (src/security.ts:48 c.store.all(), evaluated on every Redactor.text call, reached from the MCP response path src/mcp.ts:40 and the tool error path src/mcp.ts:60) are neither tracked nor woken, so they resume against a closed database. Observed throw: RangeError: Cannot use a closed database, stack security.ts:48 <- text security.ts:7 <- mcp.ts:40 and security.ts:48 <- text security.ts:7 <- mcp.ts:60. The second site is inside register()'s catch block, so the tool's own error path also throws and no isError result is produced. Contained: no unhandled rejection, no crash, no post-close writes.
reproduction: Reviewer probe outside the checkout: /tmp/rv-probe/probe2.ts patches Store.prototype to record any method invoked after Store.close(), seeds a running worker with the repo's FakeProvider/FakeAgent, starts the server, parks provider.getWorker behind a deferred, fires get_worker_logs, calls handle.stop(), then releases the deferred. Bun 1.4.2, exit 0: DRAIN drained 20ms; POST-CLOSE THROWING CALLS 2 (both store.all from security.ts:48); POST-CLOSE WRITES 0; UNHANDLED []. /tmp/rv-probe/probe-postclose.ts independently saw 3 post-close calls (get, events, all) and 0 unhandled rejections. Why guards miss it: docs/SERVE.md and tests/serve.test.ts:643 cover only wait_for_state_change, which stopWaiters does wake; no guard covers the other read-only handlers or the redactor.
recommendation: Make Store.close() set a closed flag and have read methods return a neutral result (null / []) instead of throwing, so a late reader degrades rather than fails; and/or track WorkerFiles handlers with the same Coordinator.track() accounting used for writes and snapshot the redactor secret set once so redaction never needs a post-shutdown database read.
confidence: reproduced: high for the throw (two independent probes, real SQLite and real HTTP/MCP transport); medium for user-visible impact because api.stop(true) usually force-closes the socket first and masks it

title: A repeated SIGINT/SIGTERM cannot shorten a stuck drain; the operator waits the full 60s default deadline
evidence: onSignal() returns immediately on any signal after the first (src/serve-command.ts:112), and the deadline timer is created only inside the first-signal path (src/serve-command.ts:120). defaultShutdownTimeoutMs is 60000 (src/serve-command.ts:9). A drain blocked on a non-settling provider promise, or on pushBranch bounded by SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120000, src/config.ts:53) which already exceeds the 60s shutdown deadline, therefore always runs to the deadline: the operator's repeated Ctrl-C is dropped and the process exits 70 (forcedShutdownExitCode). Under systemd with TimeoutStopSec below 60s the unit is SIGKILLed, yielding 137 instead of 70 and losing the 'Shutdown deadline exceeded' diagnostic.
reproduction: Deterministic code trace: src/serve-command.ts:112 returns before any deadline handling, and no other code path observes signals; handle.stop() is already owned by the first signal. Corroborated by the existing test tests/serve.test.ts:835, which asserts stdout.split('Shutdown requested') has length 2, i.e. the repeat is deliberately ignored, and by tests/serve.test.ts:892, where the only escape is a 400ms SWARMFORGE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS. Not separately reproduced in a spawned child.
recommendation: Treat a second signal while a drain is in progress as an escalation: shorten to a small grace deadline or exit 70 directly, which is the conventional supervisor-friendly behaviour. Leave the first-signal drain intact so durable state is still preserved on the normal path.
confidence: code-evidenced: high (deterministic from onSignal and corroborated by an existing test); the behaviour is deliberate and documented, hence LOW rather than higher

title: Metrics listener has no host allowlist and no bearer authentication on a public bind
evidence: startServer builds a second Bun.serve on SWARMFORGE_METRICS_PORT bound to the same config.SWARMFORGE_HOST with an inline fetch (src/serve.ts:182-190) that only checks `new URL(request.url).pathname === "/metrics"`. Neither the accepted-host check nor the bearer check from createHttpHandler (src/http.ts:9-29) is applied. The non-loopback token invariant lives only in config.ts superRefine (src/config.ts:135-141) and is therefore implemented on one of the two listeners. Confirmed against a live startServer with SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 and SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN set: GET /metrics with no Authorization header returned 200 (2037 bytes), with a deliberately wrong token returned 200, and with an arbitrary Host header returned 200, while GET /health on the API port returned 401. After an authenticated spawn_worker the unauthenticated body contained swarmforge_workers{team="team",state="queued"} 1, swarmforge_workers_created_total{team="team"} 1 and swarmforge_tokens_total{team="team",model="qwen",direction="input"}. docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:32 documents SWARMFORGE_HOST as the 'MCP and metrics listen interface'. No test asserts anything about authorization on the metrics port. Carried over unchanged from the deleted src/main.ts at baseline 5672ead.
reproduction: Reproduced. /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe.ts (P4) and /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe3.ts (P5) with FakeProvider/FakeAgent and an on-disk SQLite DB in /tmp; log at /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/probe-auth.log.
recommendation: Extract the host+auth gate from src/http.ts into a reusable helper and apply it to the metrics listener, or add a dedicated metrics credential plus host allowlist, and/or default a separate SWARMFORGE_METRICS_HOST to 127.0.0.1 while serving metrics through the authenticated port.

title: Exact origin equality refuses the documented TLS-terminating reverse-proxy deployment with 403 after successful auth
evidence: `const origin = request.headers.get("origin"); if (origin && origin !== url.origin) return 403`. Under a TLS-terminating proxy (the deployment src/config.ts:13-15 and docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 target: loopback bind plus SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=mcp.example.com), Bun builds the request URL as http://mcp.example.com/... from the forwarded Host header, so url.origin is http://mcp.example.com while any browser-origin client sends Origin: https://mcp.example.com. The check runs after the bearer check (line 20-29), so the operator sees a 403 on a request that authenticated successfully. Reproduced over a real socket against Bun.serve: Host: mcp.example.com with a valid bearer token and Origin: https://mcp.example.com returned HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden on /health and on /events, while the same request without Origin returned 200 and with Origin: http://mcp.example.com:8787 returned 200. tests/http.test.ts:19-31 only asserts that a hostile origin is rejected; nothing asserts the accept path.
