reproduction: Reproduced. /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe4.ts (P6, raw net socket to a live server) and /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe.ts (P2 2a, synthetic Request).
recommendation: Compare the origin host against the same accepted-host set used for the Host header rather than exact scheme/host/port equality, so a hostile page is still rejected while https-vs-http and proxy-rewritten ports stop mattering; or accept an explicit SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list.

title: Bearer comparison short-circuits on byte length, so timingSafeEqual never protects wrong-length candidates
evidence: `Buffer.byteLength(actual) !== Buffer.byteLength(desired) || !timingSafeEqual(...)` returns 401 without ever calling timingSafeEqual whenever the candidate length differs, so the 401 latency is a function of the candidate length and discloses the exact length of the configured token (src/config.ts:81 enforces only min(24)). No prefix is disclosed. In-process micro-measurement of 120000 interleaved handler calls: len8 median=0.00184ms, same-length-wrong median=0.00221ms, correct median=0.00241ms, i.e. a real but roughly 0.4 microsecond branch difference. Network exploitability was not measured and is unlikely given HTTP noise.
reproduction: Code-evidenced plus in-process measurement; /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe.ts (P1) and /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe2.ts (F3, N=120000). Not exploitable over a network in this review.
recommendation: Compare fixed-length digests instead: timingSafeEqual(sha256(actual), sha256(desired)), which removes the length branch entirely.

title: Host allowlist is compared case-sensitively, so a configured hostname in non-lowercase form can never match
evidence: The hosts set is built from c.config.SWARMFORGE_HOST and the split SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS entries with trim+filter(Boolean) but no lowercasing, while new URL().hostname is always lowercased by the WHATWG parser. config.ts:11-12 does lowercase for its loopback decision, so the two policies normalize differently. With SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=MCP.Example.COM, loadConfig succeeds and demands a token, but both http://mcp.example.com/health and http://MCP.EXAMPLE.COM/health returned 403 with a valid bearer token. Fail-closed, so this is an availability break on the exact hostname the operator configured, not a bypass.
reproduction: Reproduced. /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe2.ts (F4) and /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe.ts (P2 2h).
recommendation: Normalize with trim+toLowerCase in http.ts, or export one acceptedHosts(config) helper from config.ts and use it in both superRefine and createHttpHandler so the policy cannot drift.

title: Missing Host header throws out of the HTTP handler before any auth check, yielding an unhandled 500 and attacker-triggerable stack traces
evidence: `const url = new URL(request.url)` is not guarded. An HTTP/1.0-style request with no Host header and a relative target gives Bun a relative request.url, so the constructor throws TypeError [ERR_INVALID_URL]. This happens before the host allowlist (line 18) and the bearer check (line 20), so it is reachable unauthenticated and pre-auth by construction, and neither createHttpHandler nor the startupGate wrapper (src/serve.ts:50-61) catches it. Reproduced over a real socket: `GET /health HTTP/1.0` with no Host returned HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error and Bun wrote a full stack trace including absolute filesystem paths and http.ts line numbers to stderr. The client cannot observe the trace, so the impact is a wrong status class plus unbounded attacker-driven stack-trace logging.
reproduction: Reproduced. /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe4.ts (P6 last case).
recommendation: Wrap the parse, ideally the whole handler body, in try/catch returning 400 Bad Request, and reject early when the Host header is absent.

title: 401 responses omit the WWW-Authenticate bearer challenge
evidence: `return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 })` sets no challenge header. Every 401 observed in the probes reported www-authenticate=null, including GET /events on a live token-protected server. RFC 9110 requires a WWW-Authenticate challenge on a 401, so clients that key re-authentication off it cannot discover that a bearer credential is expected. Status-code-only assertions in tests/http.test.ts cannot catch this.
reproduction: Reproduced. /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe.ts (P2, all cases report no-WWW-Authenticate) and /tmp/sf19/probe/auth-probe3.ts (P5 www-authenticate=null).
recommendation: Add headers: { "www-authenticate": 'Bearer realm="swarmforge"' } to the 401 response.

title: SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS entries are matched case-sensitively, so valid hostname spellings (uppercase, trailing root dot, embedded port) are silently dead and every request returns a bare 403
evidence: src/http.ts:9-19 builds the allowlist Set from the raw config strings (SWARMFORGE_HOST at line 13, split/trim of SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS at lines 14-16) and compares with `hosts.has(url.hostname)` at line 18. WHATWG URL lowercases the authority, so `new URL(request.url).hostname` is always lower-case and never contains a port. src/config.ts:10-12 (`loopbackHosts`/`isLoopbackHost`) lowercases for its own comparison, proving case-insensitivity is the intended semantics. src/config.ts:16-24 (`acceptedHosts`) only checks that a token exists; it never checks that an entry is matchable.
reproduction: Real Bun.serve listener, valid bearer on every request, only the allowed_hosts spelling varies (/tmp/opencode/review20/probe/allowlist-probe.ts, log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-allowlist-probe.log): allowed_hosts="MCP.Example.Test" with Host: MCP.Example.Test -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden; allowed_hosts="Mcp.Example.Test" -> 403; allowed_hosts="mcp.example.test" -> 200 OK; allowed_hosts="mcp.example.test:8787" -> 403. Control isolating the cause: Host: LOCALHOST reaches 200 OK against the default config whose allowlist holds only lowercase `localhost` (/workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-wire-probe.log), proving normalisation happens on the wire side only.
consequence: A reverse-proxy deployment configured exactly as docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 instructs accepts the value, enforces the token, then refuses /health, /events and /mcp with 403 and no log or startup diagnostic, so the operator diagnoses a credential or networking fault instead of the accepted-host list.
recommendation: Lower-case and strip a trailing root dot from each config entry when building the set in src/http.ts (normalise IPv6 entries to bracketed form), and add a superRefine issue on SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS in src/config.ts rejecting any entry containing ':', differing from its own lower-case form, or ending in '.', so `swarmforge config validate` and startup fail loudly. Newly exposed as `server.allowed_hosts` at src/settings/load.ts:272-277.

title: Origin is compared against url.origin, so any TLS-terminating reverse proxy - the documented deployment shape - rejects every request that carries an Origin header
evidence: src/http.ts:30-32: `const origin = request.headers.get("origin"); if (origin && origin !== url.origin) return 403`. `url.origin` is derived from the plaintext listener connection plus the forwarded Host, so it is always the http backend origin. No Forwarded / X-Forwarded-Proto handling exists anywhere in the repo. The SDK's own `enableDnsRebindingProtection` is left at its default false (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js:79), so nothing downstream compensates.
reproduction: Real listener, allowed host and valid bearer on every request, only Host/Origin pairing varies (/tmp/opencode/review20/probe/allowlist-probe.ts, log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-allowlist-probe.log): Host: mcp.example.test + Origin: https://mcp.example.test -> 403; Host: mcp.example.test:443 + Origin: https://mcp.example.test -> 403; control Host: mcp.example.test + Origin: http://mcp.example.test -> 406 Not Acceptable, i.e. it passed the origin check and reached the MCP transport, proving the 403 is the origin comparison.
consequence: For the TLS-terminating proxy that docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 ('for a reverse proxy') and the README ('Deploy TLS ... externally') direct operators to use, every origin-aware client gets 403 on all routes including /health and /events, since the check precedes routing. No diagnostic distinguishes a TLS terminator from a hostile origin.
recommendation: Derive accepted origins from configuration instead of the plaintext connection: either treat Origin as advisory once the host allowlist has pinned the authority and a bearer token is configured, or add an explicit SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list and/or opt-in X-Forwarded-Proto/Forwarded scheme trust restricted to already-bearer-authenticated requests (trimming default :443/:80). If neither, document at docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 that a terminating proxy must rewrite Origin, and add the missing positive test.

title: The metrics listener enforces neither the host allowlist nor the bearer token on the same bind host the config validator protects
evidence: src/serve.ts:177-191 binds metrics to config.SWARMFORGE_HOST and serves /metrics from an inline fetch with no host validation and no credential check, unlike the API handler at src/http.ts:9-29. src/config.ts:135-141 raises the non-loopback token requirement based on acceptedHosts, which covers only the MCP surface.
reproduction: Real startServer with SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 and SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN set (/tmp/opencode/review20/probe/metrics-probe.ts, log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-metrics-probe.log): API listener 18787 -> Host: 127.0.0.1 = 401, Host: evil.example = 403; metrics listener 19090 -> Host: 127.0.0.1 = 200, Host: evil.example = 200, Host: attacker-controlled.example = 200, all with no credential, exposing team labels and worker/inference/token counters from src/metrics.ts.
consequence: A deployment satisfying every documented configuration check can still leave Prometheus telemetry world-readable on a wildcard bind; the 401/403 on the API surface creates a false impression that the deployment is authenticated.
recommendation: Route the metrics fetch through the same host allowlist (403 on a non-allowlisted Host) and/or require an explicit opt-in before binding metrics to a non-loopback SWARMFORGE_HOST; add a 403 test for an arbitrary Host on the metrics port. Documented at docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:45 ('Protect externally if public'), hence LOW rather than higher.

title: Startup banner prints an invalid URL for IPv6 binds, including the wildcard ::
evidence: src/runtime.ts:50-56 interpolates the raw host: line 50 special-cases 0.0.0.0 only, line 53 emits `http://${host}:${info.port}/mcp`. Reached from src/serve-command.ts:148-161, which passes config.SWARMFORGE_HOST unchanged while taking the port from the correctly bracketed handle.url. Contrast src/serve.ts:110-113, whose origin() brackets IPv6.

title: TOCTOU between the symlink prefix walk and the read makes the artifact allowlist advisory
evidence: checked() (files.ts:24-31) calls noSymlinks() (files.ts:32-40), which issues one provider.stat per path prefix, then a separate stat for size/isFile; readArtifact (files.ts:92-101) then performs a third, independent provider.readFile. No verified directory entry is bound to the bytes actually returned. A guest process that rewrites a checked prefix into a symlink after the walk makes SwarmForge return bytes from an arbitrary guest path as a worker artifact, contradicting docs/MCP-API.md ('Traversal and symlink paths are rejected'). Content redaction at files.ts:103-106 still applies, so this is a confinement failure rather than a proven secret disclosure.
reproduction: Reproduced locally with the repository's FakeProvider (no real guest). /tmp/rv-probe/probe.test.ts probe E: provider.stat returns a clean non-symlink file for every prefix during the checking phase; provider.readFile flips the fake to the post-check phase and returns /etc/shadow-shaped content. Observed: readArtifact returned that content with no error. Why guards/tests miss it: tests/api.test.ts:185 forces provider.stat to always report isSymlink=true, which only proves the check fires when stat itself is hostile; no test mutates the path between the walk and the read.
recommendation: Stop treating prefix stat results as a capability. Either re-verify the prefixes after the read and discard on mismatch, or have the provider resolve and read in one guest-side operation that opens each component with O_NOFOLLOW/equivalent so a single call both reads and rejects symlinked prefixes. If only mitigating, perform the walk and the read inside one bounded provider call and document the residual guest-side race.
confidence: high - reproduced against the target code via the repository's own fake-provider seam; guest-side read behavior not observed against a real Freestyle guest

title: Artifact chunk credential screen is defeated by a credential longer than the overlap pad; credential bytes are returned to the caller
evidence: readArtifact derives the overlap from only two of the four secret sources in redactorFor: pad = Math.max(4096, config.SWARMFORGE_MODEL_API_KEY.length, config.FREESTYLE_API_TOKEN.length) (src/files.ts:94-98), while the screen at src/files.ts:103 is an exact whole-secret substring match over the decoded window (Redactor.contains, src/security.ts:38-41) against the four-source set from redactorFor (src/security.ts:44-49: FREESTYLE_API_TOKEN, SWARMFORGE_MODEL_API_KEY, SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN, and every worker's server_password). SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN is the only omitted source with no schema length ceiling (src/config.ts:81, z.string().min(24).optional()). With start = max(0, offset - pad) and window length + 2*pad, any read at offset > pad truncates such a credential at the window's LEFT edge, the exact match fails, no exception is thrown, and src/files.ts:107 returns the portion inside the caller's range: up to secretLength - 4097 contiguous credential bytes. The RIGHT edge is sound because the window extends pad past the chunk end (verified). Trigger: a worker artifact larger than one chunk holds the configured SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN and the lead walks next_offset; offset=0 is refused, offset=32768 starts its window at 28672 and returns 904 bytes of the credential.
reproduction: Reproduced. Disposable detached worktree at /tmp/rev-24 (git rev-parse HEAD = target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895), official Bun 1.4.2 at /tmp/bun142, bun install --frozen-lockfile exit 0. Probe at /tmp/probe/probe.ts (outside the source checkout) uses a fake WorkerProvider with a byte-range readFile plus a real Coordinator/Store/WorkerFiles, sets SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN to a synthetic 5000-character placeholder (schema-legal, min 24, no max; the two tokens folded into pad left short), stores a 60000-byte artifact with the token at absolute bytes [0,5000), then calls readArtifact(id, 'blob.bin', 4196, 32768). Observed: pad=4096, provider window start=100 len=40960 (token truncated to its last 4900 bytes), no exception, 804 contiguous credential bytes returned whose leading characters match the token prefix. Controls in the same run that PASSED, isolating the defect to the left edge: short secret inside the chunk -> refused; the same 5000-character token at absolute byte 5000 -> refused; the token straddling the right window edge -> refused; junk high bytes (c3 28 e0 80 80 fe ff) before an ASCII secret -> still detected (rules out UTF-8 decode consumption as an alternative cause). Also verified server_password is a fixed 72 chars (src/store.ts:96, two randomUUIDs), so that omission is latent rather than exploitable.
recommendation: Derive the overlap from the live secret set so the screen and the secret set cannot drift: in readArtifact, const secrets = redactorFor(this.c).secrets().filter(Boolean); const pad = Math.max(4096, ...secrets.map((s) => Buffer.byteLength(s))); then start = Math.max(0, offset - pad). Use Buffer.byteLength rather than String.length so the pad is in bytes, matching the byte offsets used by readFile and contains. Consider screening in latin1 (byte-preserving) or scanning the raw bytes so no decode step can drop a partial match. Add a regression test that reads a second/third chunk of an artifact holding a SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN longer than the pad with the credential straddling offset - pad; the existing tests/api.test.ts:104-127 only reads offset 0 with 12-byte secrets, which cannot observe the boundary.
confidence: high on mechanism (reproduced end-to-end through the real readArtifact); medium on real-world likelihood because it requires a schema-legal but atypical SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN above 4096 bytes - documented as 'minimum 24 characters' with no documented maximum

title: prepare() outer bound is shorter than its own inner budget, so a slow-but-healthy guest livelocks in booting and its endpoint is discarded
evidence: Outer bound at coordinator.ts:461-467 is SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS + SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000+30000 = 150000ms at shipped defaults (config.ts:53,89). prepare() inner per-step timeoutMs budgets are 30000 (freestyle.ts:117 init) + 120000 (freestyle.ts:131 clone) + 30000 (freestyle.ts:144 checkout) + 30000 (freestyle.ts:180 systemctl) = 210000ms worst case. bounded() (coordinator.ts:41-59) uses Promise.race, so it rejects at 150s while the abandoned prepare() keeps running; the endpoint is never stored because store.patch(id,{endpoint}) at coordinator.ts:467 is never reached.
reproduction: Executed with Bun 1.4.2 outside the checkout, real Coordinator + local fake provider, shipped default ratios scaled 1:1000 (API=30ms, GIT_PUSH=120ms, outer bound=150ms), polling like the scheduler (/tmp/rev-wc71d/probe/threshold.ts): inner=100ms -> attempts=1 state=waiting endpoint=RECORDED; inner=149ms -> attempts=1 endpoint=RECORDED; inner=160ms -> attempts=16 state=booting endpoint=LOST; inner=210ms -> attempts=16 endpoint=LOST; inner=260ms -> attempts=16 endpoint=LOST. Staged worst-case probe converge.ts: 'prepare() attempts: 16 | completed server-side: 15 | state: booting | endpoint recorded: null'. converge-fast.ts reaches waiting in 1 attempt, isolating the bound as the cause.
recommendation: Raise the bound to exceed the sum of inner budgets (e.g. GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS + 4*API_TIMEOUT_MS), and/or pass an AbortSignal into bounded() so an abandoned attempt is cancelled rather than duplicated. Track in-flight prepare() per worker and skip retries while one is outstanding.

title: Abandoned prepare() retries run concurrently against the same VM and race each other on the shared clone staging dir and temporary Git credential
evidence: Staging path is derived only from worker_id: `${workspace}/.swarmforge/repo-clone-${w.worker_id}` (freestyle.ts:126); the clone command begins `rm -rf <staging> && git clone ... && mv <staging> <repository>` (freestyle.ts:129); credential files are fixed guest paths ['/opt/swarmforge/git-auth','/opt/swarmforge/git-secret'] (freestyle.ts:193) written before the action and unconditionally `rm -f`'d afterwards (freestyle.ts:229-240). Because Promise.race in F1 leaves the abandoned prepare() running and step() retries on the next tick (coordinator.ts:510-526), two prepare() calls execute concurrently on one VM.
reproduction: Executed, Bun 1.4.2, faithful local model of both shared guest paths (/tmp/rev-wc71d/probe/race.ts), inner 660ms vs outer bound 430ms: 'prepare starts: p1,p2 | maxConcurrent: 2 | clone failures: 2 | p1: credential file deleted by a concurrent prepare (owner=p2) | p2: credential file deleted by a concurrent prepare (owner=null)'. stack.ts at sustained scale: 150 attempts over the provisioning window, 'attempts whose rm -rf staging hit a live clone: 1'.
recommendation: Apply the single-flight fix from F1, and/or make the staging directory and credential paths attempt-scoped (random suffix) so an abandoned attempt cannot collide with its successor. Have withGitAuth verify the credential still belongs to the current attempt before removing it.

title: createWorker's slug pre-check is not atomic, so a create-timeout can produce duplicate VMs for one worker
evidence: createWorker does `const existing = await this.getWorker(slug); if (existing) return existing;` (freestyle.ts:46-47) then vms.create (freestyle.ts:48). Check-then-create is racy. The create is bounded by SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS (coordinator.ts:457) while the freestyle SDK backgrounds long requests and polls (node_modules/freestyle/dist/client.js, BACKGROUND_AFTER_SECS=5), so a slow create can outlive the bound and remain running provider-side. The next tick re-enters createWorker; if the first VM is not yet visible to vms.get(slug) the pre-check passes and a second VM is created with the same slug and metadata.worker_id.
reproduction: NOT reproduced against the real Freestyle API (would require real infrastructure, out of scope). Coordinator-side mechanism reproduced with a local fake modelling slug-visibility lag (/tmp/rev-wc71d/probe/dup-create.ts): 'VMs created for ONE worker record: 2', 'max concurrent createWorker: 3'. recover() (coordinator.ts:365-396) later surfaces the extra VM as a recovery_required orphan rather than losing it, so residual impact is a duplicate billable VM plus a spurious recovery record.
recommendation: Pass an idempotency key to vms.create if supported; otherwise make createWorker single-flight per worker (same fix as F1/F2), and treat a same-slug VM found during recovery as adoption rather than orphan creation.

title: resume_worker silently no-ops forever once previous_state becomes "paused" (pause intent racing an out-of-band guest pause)
evidence: applyControl pause sets previous_state: w.state with no guard (851-855); resume transitions to w.previous_state ?? "ready" (861); the running/waiting branch of step transitions the worker to paused without re-checking a recorded intent (497-503); runTick never steps paused workers (344-349); queueMessage repairs previous_state only when it is terminal (226-237); store.transition emits no state event when the state is unchanged (src/store.ts:146-158).

title: Guest discovered stopped keeps a stale deadline_at, so follow-up messages are accepted then failed instantly
evidence: The stopped-VM reconcile branch transitions to recovery_required with only {error} (429-432), unlike every other recovery_required transition which clears deadline_at (573-577, 800-804, 919-921, 936-941). The follow-up transition for failed/recovery_required does not reset deadline_at (238-243) and the absolute-deadline check runs before any provisioning work (452-455). title: Event log file mode is never re-asserted, so a pre-existing loose-mode log keeps its permissions and keeps receiving worker prompts
evidence: appendFileSync(path, `${line}\n`, { mode: 0o600 }) is the only mode control on the append path. Node/Bun apply appendFileSync's `mode` through open(...,'a',mode), which only takes effect on creation, and there is no chmod on this path. renameSync(path, `${path}.1`) at src/runtime.ts:207 preserves the same mode onto the rotated backup. The sibling database does re-assert: src/store.ts:21 calls chmodSync(path, 0o600) unconditionally on every construction. Reached from src/serve.ts:192 via eventLogger(coordinator, `${config.SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH}.log`). Appended lines carry event payloads, which include worker prompts.
reproduction: Reproduced locally with Bun 1.4.2 against the target checkout using a local probe (/tmp/sfrev/probe/p6.ts, exit 0): create a Store, record an event whose data contains a prompt marker, pre-create <DB>.log at 0644 to model a backup restore, drive eventLogger three times, then print modes. Output: swarmforge.sqlite-shm 0600, swarmforge.sqlite 0600, swarmforge.sqlite-wal 0600, swarmforge.sqlite.log 0644, and db 0600 after a second Store(). Trigger in practice: an operator restores/copies the database directory from a backup, or points SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH at a file in a directory they manage by hand.
recommendation: Mirror the database pattern in eventLogger: chmod the log to 0o600 when it exists before/after the first append, and apply the same to the rotated ${path}.1 after renameSync. This removes the asymmetry with src/store.ts:21.
impact: Bounded in the default layout because src/store.ts:19 creates the parent directory 0700, which prevents other local users traversing into it. Becomes real when SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH is placed in a directory that is not 0700 (e.g. a 0755 home directory or an operator-managed /var/lib path): the database is 0600 while the adjacent log holding the same prompts is world-readable. Prompts are credential-free by design, so this is a permissions/consistency defect, not a credential leak.

title: An unrecognized /session/status response shape is read as 'the turn finished', silently completing a worker mid-generation
evidence: inspect() reads sessionStatus(status.data?.[w.opencode_session_id]?.type). For any body that is not a record keyed by session id (null, array, string, non-status body) the index yields undefined and sessionStatus() returns 'idle' at line 184, which coordinator.ts:560 treats as settled. title: URL credential scrubbing misses username-only userinfo and every non-http(s) scheme
evidence: The URL userinfo rule in Redactor.text matches only when the scheme is http or https AND the userinfo contains a colon separating username from password. Two common shapes fail at least one condition: (a) a username-only URL credential, i.e. a bearer token in the username position with an empty password, the form used by Git/GitHub personal access token clone remotes; (b) any non-http scheme with a username:password@host userinfo - ssh, git+ssh, postgres, redis, mongodb+srv, amqp and file were all verified unredacted. Reached from every Redactor.text consumer: redactedSettings (src/settings/inspect.ts:127,132), redactedText (:97), redact (:145), serve command diagnostics (src/serve-command.ts:151), event log (src/runtime.ts:196,199), MCP responses and error text (src/mcp.ts:40,59), and the /events SSE stream (src/http.ts:45). SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_URL is added to the secret set only by commandRedactor (src/serve-command.ts:47); the redactedSettings path used by `config show` and `serve --check-config` does not include it (SECRET_KEYS, src/settings/inspect.ts:7-11).
reproduction: A config file whose git.ssh.push_url carries a username-only URL credential is printed byte-for-byte by both `bun src/cli.ts config show --config ...` and `bun src/cli.ts serve --check-config --config ...`: the reported SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_URL value still contains the token. The same happens for an ssh URL carrying a username and password. The classic http(s) username:password@host form IS redacted in the same runs, proving this regex is the only guard for the other shapes.
recommendation: Scrub any userinfo regardless of scheme or presence of a password component: match an optional scheme followed by userinfo up to the separating at-sign and replace the whole userinfo with the redaction marker. Additionally register SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_URL in the loader credential context (or in SECRET_KEYS) so redactedSettings treats the entire value as a credential.
guard_analysis: tests/serve.test.ts:779-806 and tests/inspect.test.ts:97 exercise only the colon-bearing http(s) form. A third-party credential echoed by a provider or SDK error is outside the known-secret set by definition, which is exactly what this generic rule exists for (stated intent at src/serve-command.ts:36-37).

title: Query-parameter credential scrubbing covers only four names
evidence: The query-parameter rule in Redactor.text is an exact allowlist of four parameter names (token, generic key, underscored API key, password) and requires the name to be preceded by a query separator and followed immediately by an equals sign. Verified unredacted: the access_token, refresh_token and id_token names; the hyphenated and unseparated API-key spellings; secret, client_secret, bearer, auth, sig and the X-Amz-Signature header parameter. The four allowlisted names are correctly scrubbed. The hyphenated API-key spelling is the Azure/OpenAI convention and sig / X-Amz-Signature are SigV4, all commonly echoed in SDK error text.
reproduction: A probe over redactedText(settings, ...) and commandRedactor(config).text(...) with thirteen dummy third-party query shapes returned byte-identical (unredacted) output for twelve of them; only the allowlisted password name was scrubbed. See /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/rv33-probes.log.

title: The known-secret base64 variant matches only at 3-byte-aligned offsets and misses the URL-safe alphabet
evidence: The variant set built in Redactor.text is the raw secret, its percent-encoding, and its standard base64 encoding. Standard base64 is a stream of 3-byte groups, so a secret's encoded form appears as a literal substring of a larger base64 payload only when the secret starts at a byte offset that is a multiple of three. Consequence 1: a base64 blob embedding the secret after a non-aligned prefix is not scrubbed, concretely an HTTP Basic credential whose username prefix length is not a multiple of three. Consequence 2: the URL-safe base64 alphabet is never generated, so when the standard encoding of a secret contains the non-URL-safe characters, its URL-safe form is not recognised.
reproduction: Alignment sweep with a 24-character dummy token: prefix lengths 0 and 3 (aligned) redacted; prefix lengths 1, 2, 4 and 5 returned unchanged and base64-decoded straight back to the full token. An HTTP Basic credential built from a short username prefix plus the token was returned unchanged. URL-safe alphabet: a dummy token whose standard base64 contains the non-URL-safe characters was redacted in standard base64 but NOT in the URL-safe form. Note the codebase's own Basic prefix is the OpenCode username at src/providers/opencode.ts:66, nine bytes and therefore aligned, so the built-in path is safe by coincidence of prefix length rather than by construction.
recommendation: Add the URL-safe base64 form, and for each of the three possible byte offsets add the corresponding partial encodings derived from base64 of the secret preceded by one and by two filler bytes with the leading groups stripped. Consider the hex form as well.
guard_analysis: tests/serve.test.ts:731-736 asserts only the standalone base64 string of a token, i.e. offset zero with no padding conflict. No test embeds a secret in a prefixed base64 payload, and none exercises the URL-safe alphabet.

title: excerptText normalizes after redacting, so a whitespace-bearing credential is reconstructed verbatim

A credential that itself contains a space is therefore not matched in the raw input but is reassembled in the output. src/config.ts:28 and :47 accept any non-empty credential, so a credential containing a space is valid configuration.

Partially mitigating: the excerpt is redacted a second time by redactor.value at the MCP boundary (src/mcp.ts:40), so the served surface is protected, though the unredacted value still lives in process memory and is what the excerpt consumers render.

title: A one-to-three character credential defeats the generic query scrub and disables artifact retrieval
evidence: The known-secret substring pass at lines 7-16 runs before the generic URL and query rules at lines 18-22, so a short credential can rewrite a parameter name before the generic rule can match it. The credential settings are validated as a one-character-minimum string at src/config.ts:28 and src/config.ts:47, so a one-character credential is valid configuration. Consumed by the artifact path guard at src/files.ts:70 and the artifact content guard at src/files.ts:103.
reproduction: Confidentiality effect: with a one-character dummy secret, an upstream API-key parameter's value was left fully visible, whereas the same input with a normal-length secret set was correctly redacted. recommendation: Treat a next token beginning with '-' as a missing value inside value(), mirroring src/cli/arguments.ts:110; the same guard also fixes the empty-value case.

title: --version/--help discard all remaining arguments; -h/-V undocumented
evidence: parseArguments returns {kind:"version"} at src/cli/arguments.ts:145 and {kind:"help"} at :144 (and :106-108 for `config --help`) before the rest of argv is scanned, so trailing unknown arguments are silently ignored (exit 0), unlike the strict unknown-argument refusal elsewhere. usage (src/cli.ts:37-38,54-55) lists only --version/--help although -V/-h are accepted (src/cli/arguments.ts:41,145).
reproduction: Pure parser probe: parseArguments(["-V","--nonsense"]) = {kind:"version"}; parseArguments(["--version","status"]) = {kind:"version"}; both exit 0 through src/cli.ts:314-321.
recommendation: Reject leftover arguments after help/version with a usage error, or document that they are ignored, and list -h/-V in usage.

title: Interactive dashboard re-prints the unredacted endpoint after its first refresh
evidence: client.overview() returns { url } from the raw url argument (client.ts:88). src/cli.ts:160 scrubs data.url once, but runDashboard's refresh() replaces the whole object with a fresh client.overview() result (tui.ts:56) and renderOverview prints `MCP  ${data.url}` (overview.ts:156). The scrub is never re-applied, so the raw endpoint is on screen from the first 5s poll (tui.ts:125) onward. Rendered line shape: a `MCP  ` prefix followed by the loopback endpoint with its query string intact, then the metrics segment.
reproduction: Probe /tmp/rev40/probe/tui-url.ts (real createHttpHandler server, real connectSwarmForge, real runDashboard) reported booleans: initial frame marker present = false, post-refresh frame marker present = true. Probe /tmp/rev40/probe/pty-e2e.ts ran the real `bun src/cli.ts status --url <endpoint carrying the marker>` under a real pty (script -qec) past the 5s poll: transcript marker present = true. Trigger: operator runs `swarmforge status` on a TTY while the resolved endpoint carries a bearer value in its query string (a token-named parameter) or in its user-information component, supplied via --url or client.url. Consequence: the control-plane bearer value is rendered to the terminal and scrollback for as long as the dashboard runs. Probes assert on a boolean marker match rather than the marker text.
recommendation: Separate the connection URL from the display URL: either let connectSwarmForge accept a caller-supplied display URL, or re-apply scrub(settings, ...) to `data` inside runDashboard's refresh() immediately after `data = await client.overview()`. Add a test that drives runDashboard with a client whose overview() returns a credential-bearing url and asserts no rendered frame contains it.

title: Dashboard error banner is not scrubbed with the resolved client credential context
evidence: runDashboard catches refresh (tui.ts:76-81), inspect (92-97) and control (110-115) errors itself and assigns the raw message to `message` (tui.ts:77, :93, :111), which is rendered via safeTerminalText (tui.ts:48). safeTerminalText strips control characters only and performs no credential redaction. Because the error never propagates out of runDashboard, the outer catch at src/cli.ts:180-187 - the only place the resolved credential context is applied - never runs. The same lines at src/cli.ts:184-186 do scrub, and src/cli.ts:181-183 documents the intent.
reproduction: Probe /tmp/rev40/probe/tui-error.ts drove the real runDashboard with a client whose overview() throws an error embedding a synthetic marker: banner contains marker = true. Banner shape: a `Refresh failed:` prefix, a remote refusal phrase, then a bearer scheme and the marker. Transport feasibility confirmed by /tmp/rev40/probe/transport-error.ts with a real StreamableHTTPClientTransport: the SDK error message is a streamable-HTTP POST failure phrase that embeds the remote response body, and that body contained the marker (message contains marker = true). Trigger: any refresh, inspect, or pause/resume/cancel/destroy failure after the initial successful overview, where the remote failure text carries the bearer value. Consequence: the control-plane bearer reaches the terminal whenever the server or an intermediary proxy echoes the received Authorization header in an error body.
recommendation: Pass the resolved client settings or a scrub callback into runDashboard and apply it to every message before rendering, wrapping the assignments at tui.ts:77, :93 and :111 in scrub(settings, ...). Add a test that enters runDashboard with a rejecting client and asserts the credential is absent from every frame.

title: config show emits no structured report for any failure except server value validation
evidence: reportConfigShow calls resolveClientSettings at line 247 outside the try; the try at 249-264 wraps only resolveServerSettings, and its catch rethrows anything that is not a SettingsError. prepare() (src/settings/load.ts:725-774) raises config_not_found, config_invalid, env_file_not_found and env_file_invalid, and resolveClientSettings (src/settings/load.ts:866-897) raises invalid_client. Only invalid_config, raised by the server resolver, reaches the structured server:{ok:false,code,message,hint} branch.
reproduction: Reproduced. `swarmforge config show --config typo.toml` with `[server] prot = 8787` -> exit=1, stdout empty, stderr 'SwarmForge: Invalid configuration file ...: server: Unrecognized key: "prot"'. Same empty-stdout exit=1 for malformed TOML, for env_file = "missing.env", for a non-assignment line in the env file, for client.url = "ftp://host/mcp", and for SWARMFORGE_CONFIG pointing at an absent file. Control: a valid document with an incomplete server does produce the JSON report.
recommendation: Resolve both surfaces inside one guarded block; catch SettingsError from the client resolution as well and emit {client:{ok:false,code,message,hint},server:{...}}, keeping the non-SettingsError rethrow. SettingsError.message is already credential- and control-character-free (src/settings/load.ts:49-62).

title: config path omits the config file's own env_file and never reports env-file existence
evidence: reportConfigPath derives env_files only from command.envFiles, i.e. the --env-file flags captured in src/cli/arguments.ts:118-121. The env_file declared by the document is read only inside prepare() (src/settings/load.ts:751-758), which config path never calls. This contradicts the command's own doc comment at src/cli.ts:209-210 ('the environment files layered on it') and README.md:77.
reproduction: Reproduced. With a config file containing `schema_version = 1` and `env_file = "secrets.env"`: `swarmforge config path --config withenvfile.toml` -> exit=0, {"config_path":"/tmp/.../withenvfile.toml","exists":true,"env_files":[]}. The listed secrets.env is absent, and `config validate` on the same file then exits 1 with no JSON. The explicitly listed --env-file entries carry no existence flag either.
recommendation: Read the selected document's env_file in the path branch and prepend anchorPath(env_file, dirname(configPath), homeDirectory(process.env)) to env_files, with a per-entry existence flag; fall back to today's output plus a notes field if parsing fails. Minimum acceptable change: amend the doc comment, --help and README.md:77 to state that env_files lists only --env-file flags.

title: serve --check-config reports ok:true for deployments startServer refuses at startup steps 2 and 3
evidence: The --check-config branch (src/cli.ts:195-200) only repeats the ':memory:' refusal, and the import('./serve-command') that would reach startServer is placed after the early return (src/cli.ts:204). startServer refuses first at src/serve.ts:161 via acquireProcessLock, which throws 'Another SwarmForge process owns this database' (src/runtime.ts:147-152), and then at src/serve.ts:163-166 with 'Instance ID differs from persisted database owner'. docs/SERVE.md:33-34 lists both as startup validation steps and docs/CONFIGURATION.md:225-226 requires a serve command to keep the single-database and instance-ID rules, while README.md:80 and src/cli.ts:52-53 present --check-config as the preflight verification.
reproduction: Reproduced. (a) Created a durable data/swarmforge.sqlite whose settings.instance_id was 'blue' against a config declaring [workspace] instance_id = "green": `swarmforge serve --check-config --config c.toml` -> exit=0, {"ok":true,...}. (b) Held LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on data/swarmforge.sqlite.lock from a live Bun process: the same command again returned exit=0 with {"ok":true,...}. serve itself was not started.
recommendation: In the --check-config branch, when the database file already exists, open it read-only and compare settings.instance_id with the resolved SWARMFORGE_INSTANCE_ID, failing with startServer's message; then attempt a non-blocking flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on <DB_PATH>.lock and refuse when it is held. Both are read-only, so the 'no database, lock file or listener' promise holds. Document in --help which steps remain unverified (port availability, recovery).

title: config validate and serve --check-config report ok:true for an invalid client endpoint
evidence: reportValidation calls only resolveServerSettings, so the client surface (fields at src/settings/load.ts:76-89, validation at 866-897) is never resolved. Neither docs/CONFIGURATION.md nor --help states that validation is server-only. Related: a bearer token set only as server.api_token is never surfaced as client.values.token, because client.token is a distinct config key.
reproduction: Reproduced. `swarmforge config validate --config serverok.toml` where the file declares client.url = "ftp://bad.invalid/mcp" and an otherwise complete server -> exit=0, {"ok":true,"config_path":"/tmp/.../serverok.toml",...}. `swarmforge config show` on the same file -> exit=1 with empty stdout, so no command reports the invalid endpoint in the structured redacted form.
recommendation: Resolve client settings in reportValidation too and include the redacted result under a client key, or add client_ok:false with a client_error.code. Keep values/sources as the primary server payload so existing consumers do not change.

title: config path reports exists:true when the selected config path is a directory
evidence: existsSync(path) performs no regular-file test, so any existing filesystem entry satisfies the 'whether it exists' field README.md:77 advertises.
reproduction: Reproduced. `swarmforge config path --config adir` -> exit=0, {"config_path":"/tmp/.../adir","exists":true,"env_files":[]}, while `config validate --config adir` fails with 'Cannot read ...: EISDIR'.
recommendation: Use statSync(path, {throwIfNoEntry:false})?.isFile() ?? false for the exists field, or rename it to present and add an is_file flag.

title: Interactive dashboard re-prints the raw, unredacted MCP endpoint after every refresh
evidence: cli.ts:160 scrubs data.url once via scrub(settings, endpoint) before runDashboard; tui.ts:56 replaces the whole data object with client.overview() on the first poll (5s default, cli.ts:167) or on 'r'. client.ts:88 returns url straight from the connectSwarmForge closure, i.e. the raw endpoint. renderOverview prints it at overview.ts:156, and overview.ts:211-213 applies neither redaction nor control-char sanitization. resolveClientSettings (settings/load.ts:871-891) validates only the scheme, so userinfo and credential query parameters are accepted; cli.ts:157-159 and tests/settings.test.ts:949 confirm this shape is deliberately scrubbed elsewhere. Probe g2.ts used a fixture endpoint carrying both a userinfo component and a credential query parameter: frame 1's header equalled the production Redactor output (both components replaced by its placeholder) while every post-poll frame equalled the raw fixture, and both raw components were present in the post-refresh byte stream, redrawn every second. Consequence: the credential is printed in clear text, defeating the CLI's own redaction.
reproduction: cd /tmp/opencode/rev-42/probe && bun run g2.ts (fake MCP client, no server/network); exits 0 and reports frame1 redacted, post-refresh frame unredacted.
recommendation: Keep the display endpoint out of the refreshable payload: drop url from OverviewData in client.ts and pass the scrubbed display URL from cli.ts into runDashboard, or re-apply the scrub in tui.refresh() (data = { ...(await client.overview()), url: displayUrl }).

title: renderOverview applies no terminal control-character sanitization
evidence: overview.ts:211-213 only clips lines (and skips clipping any line containing ESC[). safeTerminalText (overview.ts:81) is applied to every detail line (overview.ts:274) and to message (tui.ts:48) but never to the overview body. Probes D/H confirmed raw ESC/OSC survives renderOverview. Reachability against a compliant server is constrained and stated honestly: idSchema (domain.ts:24-28) restricts worker_id/team_id/task_id, state is an enum, and the WHATWG URL parser rejects an endpoint containing raw control bytes (verified), so today's reachable vector is a non-SwarmForge or compromised MCP endpoint accepted via --url; reported as defense-in-depth, not a live injection against SwarmForge itself.
reproduction: cd /tmp/opencode/rev-42/probe && bun run tui-probe.ts (probe D) and bun run url-probe.ts (probe H); both exit 0 with raw ESC in the rendered overview.
recommendation: Map overview lines through safeTerminalText before clipping (as the detail view does) and sanitize the header data.url the same way.

title: Terminal state (alt screen, hidden cursor, raw mode) restored only on the keypress quit path
evidence: The enter sequence is written at tui.ts:121 and the restore sequence exists only inside stop() at tui.ts:136, reachable only from the keypress handler (tui.ts:140). The await at tui.ts:123 is not wrapped in try/finally and no process signal handlers exist. Probe E: process.listenerCount for SIGTERM, SIGINT, exit and uncaughtException was 0 before and during an active dashboard session. In raw mode Ctrl-C arrives as a keypress, so the keypress handler is the only exit path.
reproduction: cd /tmp/opencode/rev-42/probe && bun run tui-probe.ts (probe E); exits 0 and prints the listener counts.
recommendation: Register SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers that call the existing idempotent stop() (the stopped flag already prevents a double restore) and wrap the render/interval work in try/finally so the terminal is restored on any exit.

title: Confirmed control action can be overwritten by an older in-flight poll snapshot
evidence: A poll refresh passes the !busy check at tui.ts:60 and blocks inside await client.worker(id) (line 63) while the user confirms a destroy. control() then calls refresh() at tui.ts:107, which no-ops because refreshing is already true, so control() finishes first and the older snapshot is written afterwards at tui.ts:65. The !busy re-check at line 64 is evaluated after the await that already started, so it cannot order the writes; the id guard only prevents a worker switch.
reproduction: cd /tmp/opencode/rev-42/probe && bun run tui-probe.ts (probe A, gated fake client.worker); exits 0 and reports the last detail frame matching /RUNNING/ and containing 'p pause' after a confirmed destroy.
recommendation: Stamp detail refreshes with a monotonic sequence number and discard results older than the last applied one, or ignore state/last_activity_at regressions for the same worker.

title: Destroy confirmation is never re-validated against the current worker state
evidence: The confirmation branch calls control('destroy') directly (tui.ts:145), bypassing the availableActions(detail.worker.state) check used by every other action key at tui.ts:177. confirmation is cleared only by n/escape (line 146) and at the start of control() (line 102); nothing invalidates it when detail changes.
reproduction: cd /tmp/opencode/rev-42/probe && bun run url-probe.ts (probe C2, poll interval 10ms); exits 0, reporting 5 consecutive frames still asking to destroy a destroyed worker and control calls === ['destroy'].
recommendation: Clear confirmation in refresh() when the refreshed state no longer offers destroy, and re-check availableActions in the confirmation branch before dispatching.

title: Ctrl-D in the detail view arms the destroy confirmation
evidence: Action matching tests key.name === 'd' with no key.ctrl check; the guard at tui.ts:140 special-cases only ctrl+c and q. readline reports Ctrl-D as {name:'d', ctrl:true} (verified with node:readline emitKeypressEvents over a PassThrough). The confirmation prompt names no worker, so the target is not identifiable at the moment of the decision; damage still requires y.
reproduction: cd /tmp/opencode/rev-42/probe && bun run ctrld2.ts; exits 0 and reports Ctrl-D armed the destroy confirmation.
recommendation: Ignore keys with key.ctrl || key.meta in the action branches and include the worker id in the confirmation prompt.

title: Unauthenticated /metrics render is O(workers x events) and starves the event loop
evidence: render() iterates every retained worker (store.all(), no DELETE anywhere in src/store.ts) and issues 5 SQL statements each; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for the per-worker event GROUP BY and the per-dispatch result.received lookup both return SCAN events (events has only a PK on id, src/store.ts:27). Measured single-scrape cost: 2000 retained workers = 2100 ms and 10003 statements in-process; via the real listener, concurrent MCP /health latency during the scrape was 44-50 ms (250 workers), 535-562 ms (1000), 7679-10312 ms (2000), 20801-23132 ms (4000) across two runs. Bun serves MCP and metrics on one event loop, so MCP calls, reconciliation and turn deadlines stall for the whole render.
reproduction: /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe-render-cost.ts <N> and /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe-blocking.ts <N> against a temp-dir SQLite seeded with N completed workers; probe-queryplan.ts prints the query plans. No real provider or network service used. Logs: /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/probe-blocking-scaling.log, listener.out, wildcard.out.
recommendation: Replace the per-worker loop with a few set-based GROUP BY aggregates over workers/events, add CREATE INDEX events_worker_type ON events(worker_id,type), cache the rendered exposition for a few seconds, and persist result timing on the dispatch row to remove the json_extract scan.

title: Metrics listener has no authentication and no Host validation and reuses SWARMFORGE_HOST
evidence: The metrics Bun.serve handler only tests pathname === /metrics (src/serve.ts:178-192); the MCP listener enforces a Host allowlist and a timing-safe bearer check (src/http.ts:11-28). SWARMFORGE_HOST is the only bind variable for both listeners and src/config.ts:142-150 only requires the ports to differ. Reproduced: loopback config with SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN set returned 200 on :9090/metrics with no Authorization header, with a wrong bearer, and with Host: attacker.example.com, while :8787/health returned 401 and 403 respectively. With SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 the metrics port answered 200 on non-loopback 172.17.0.1 while /health answered 403. Payload exposes allowlisted team IDs, model name, state counts and token volumes.
reproduction: /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe-listener.ts (loopback + hostile Host, no/wrong auth) and /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe-wildcard.ts (SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0, non-loopback reachability, team bucketing). Synthetic token; no real credentials.
recommendation: Add SWARMFORGE_METRICS_HOST defaulting to 127.0.0.1 and bind the metrics listener to it; apply the same Host allowlist (and optionally SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN) inside the metrics handler; state the auth posture in docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.

title: swarmforge_tokens_total{model} is hardcoded to SWARMFORGE_MODEL_NAME and ignores the recorded usage.model
evidence: src/metrics.ts:79-85 labels every observation with config.SWARMFORGE_MODEL_NAME, but src/coordinator.ts:546-556 persists m.model ?? configured name into usage.model (schema src/store.ts:30). store.tokens() (src/store.ts:323-353) has no GROUP BY model, so the recorded column is never surfaced. Reproduced: usage rows written with model some-other-model-9000 exported as swarmforge_tokens_total{model=qwen}.
reproduction: Seeded usage rows with a non-configured model in /tmp/sfrev/probe/probe-wildcard.ts and read back /metrics.
recommendation: Add a store aggregate grouped by usage.model and use it as the label value, or document that the label is the configured model rather than the recorded one.

title: buildConfig ignores the `root` argument, so packaging another source tree silently ships this repository's code
evidence: buildConfig hardcodes entrypoints: [join(repositoryRoot, "src", "cli.ts")], while packageVersion (scripts/build.ts:94), repositoryCommit (scripts/build.ts:110) and packageCli (scripts/package.ts:272-286) honour an options.root parameter. Version/commit come from `root`; code always comes from repositoryRoot.
reproduction: Bun 1.4.2, /tmp/probe/root-probe.ts: created /tmp/probe/altroot with package.json version 9.9.9-alt plus one git commit, then called packageCli({ root: "/tmp/probe/altroot", outDir: "/tmp/probe/altdist" }) -> exit 0, produced swarmforge-v9.9.9-alt-linux-x64-glibc.tar.gz and metadata-9.9.9-alt.json with commit f1d7b3d2..., while the archived binary is this repository's src/cli.ts build (82,695,648 bytes; --help prints this repo's usage).
recommendation: Thread root into buildConfig and use join(root, "src", "cli.ts"), or remove the root parameter so the mismatch cannot be expressed.
guard_gap: packageCli's executable.version !== version check (scripts/package.ts:287) compares two values derived from the same root, so it is self-consistent; verifyArchive only cross-checks define'd strings, the digest and the executable's own --version/--help. No test or CLI path passes root, so impact is latent rather than live in CI.

title: SHA256SUMS covers only the executable, leaving the shipped version/commit metadata unverified by the documented install step
evidence: checksums() emits one line for the executable only; README.md:50-52 teaches `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` as the operator's verification of the downloaded archive.
reproduction: Code-evidenced: a repacked archive whose metadata-<version>.json was edited passes `sha256sum -c` because the manifest never covers that file. Not executed (would require building a tampered archive).
recommendation: Add a manifest line for the metadata file and extend verifyArchive's expectedFiles and checksum expectations accordingly.
guard_gap: verifyArchive validates metadata against the executable inside the same archive, so nothing binds the metadata bytes to the shipped digest; CI catches a repack, the operator-facing post-download check does not.

title: Build provenance ignores a dirty worktree, so a modified checkout is stamped with a clean HEAD commit
evidence: repositoryCommit() validates only that `git -C root rev-parse HEAD` exits 0 and yields 40 hex chars; no `git status --porcelain` check exists in scripts/build.ts, scripts/package.ts or the release workflow.
reproduction: Code-evidenced (not executed in CI, where checkouts are clean): running `bun run build` from a checkout with uncommitted edits records HEAD, which does not describe the shipped source; the workflow cross-check `--help | grep "build $(git rev-parse HEAD)"` compares against the same HEAD and would also pass.
recommendation: Check worktree cleanliness before compiling and either refuse to package a dirty tree or record a dirty flag in the metadata; enforce it inside packageCli so all callers get it.
guard_gap: No cleanliness guard exists; scripts/build.ts:104-107 documents the commit as the operator's mapping back to source, which a dirty build silently invalidates.

title: Duplicated, unused advertisedPlatform constant in scripts/build.ts invites silent drift
evidence: scripts/build.ts:25 exports advertisedPlatform = "linux-x64-glibc" with no importer anywhere (grep over src/tests/scripts); the live copy is scripts/package.ts:40, used by archiveName (scripts/package.ts:67) and buildMetadata (scripts/package.ts:97).
reproduction: Code-evidenced: editing scripts/build.ts:25 changes no archive name, metadata field or test outcome; tests/packaging.test.ts asserts compileTarget but not the platform literal.
recommendation: Delete the dead export in scripts/build.ts or have scripts/package.ts import it from a single source.
guard_gap: No test binds the archive name or metadata platform to a single definition, so a change applied to the wrong copy passes CI.

title: verifyArchive accepts non-regular archive members and executes an out-of-tree symlink target
evidence: archiveListing (126) parses only tar -tzf names; stat() at 187 follows symlinks; run([binary,'--version']) at 232 and [binary,'--help'] at 237 execute whatever the path resolves to. Reproduced: archive with swarmforge -> /tmp/sf-probe/outside/swarmforge plus matching SHA256SUMS/metadata returned VERIFIED_OK (exit 0), and the out-of-tree target appended OUTSIDE-EXEC to a marker file twice while verification ran.
reproduction: tar member 'swarmforge' of type symlink to an out-of-tree 0755 file; SHA256SUMS/metadata computed over the link target; bun -e "verifyArchive({archivePath, expectedVersion:'0.1.0'})" exits 0. Probes /tmp/sf-probe/hostile.tar.gz, probe1.ts, probe5.ts (log: .swarmforge/logs/review-45-archive-verification.log).
recommendation: Before extraction, reject any member whose tar type is not a regular file; after extraction assert lstat().isFile() for every expected path and never stat/exec through a link. Keep GNU tar's traversal rejection as defence in depth.

title: Permission check masks setuid/setgid/sticky bits, certifying a setuid-root binary as 0755
evidence: (await stat(binary)).mode & 0o777 strips 0o4000/0o2000/0o1000 before comparing to 0o755; metadata mode at 224 is a string comparison against the literal '0755'. Reproduced: 4755 archive verified OK (SETUID_ARCHIVE_VERIFIED), extracted file is -rwsr-xr-x while metadata.executable.mode says 0755.
reproduction: Package a member with mode 4755 plus self-consistent SHA256SUMS/metadata; verifyArchive returns success and `stat -c %a` on the extracted tree shows 4755.
recommendation: Compare the full mode (mode & 0o7777) to 0o755 and reject any archive whose recorded member mode carries setuid/setgid/sticky.

title: Whitespace-only archive members are dropped, so the exact three-file listing check can be bypassed
evidence: Names are .trim()ed then filtered to length > 0 before comparison at 170. Reproduced: archive with the three expected members plus a member named '  ' extracted successfully and verified, returning files=[SHA256SUMS, metadata-0.1.0.json, swarmforge].
reproduction: Add a fourth tar member whose name is two spaces; verifyArchive still reports the archive as containing exactly the expected files.
recommendation: Normalize names without trimming to empty and explicitly reject any member whose normalized name is empty instead of filtering it away.

title: prepareReleaseAssets never checks the loose SHA256SUMS/metadata against the verified archive, and findFile selection is readdir-ordered and recursive
evidence: findFile (356) returns the first name match at any depth. Reproduced: a directory holding a valid archive plus an all-zero-digest SHA256SUMS and a 1-byte metadata-0.1.0.json returned PREPARED_OK with all three listed as release assets; a second probe selected nested/SHA256SUMS over the flat layout. The draft job then uploads those loose files (release.yml:153-159).
reproduction: Build an asset directory from a valid archive and replace the standalone SHA256SUMS/metadata with self-inconsistent content; prepareReleaseAssets succeeds and reports them as the assets to publish.
recommendation: Digest-compare the loose SHA256SUMS and metadata JSON against the copies extracted from the verified archive and reject any mismatch; restrict findFile to the flat download-artifact layout with deterministic ordering and duplicate rejection.

title: No digest is published for the downloadable archive; release notes tell users to verify with a manifest that cannot check the downloaded files
evidence: scripts/package.ts:75-77 checksums() emits exactly one line for the extracted executable ('<64 hex>  swarmforge'); :304 writes dist/SHA256SUMS from it; :315-319 copies the same into the archive; :242 and :351 compute PackagedRelease.archiveSha256 but only return it on stdout - it is never written to any file under dist/. release.yml:157-159 attaches only swarmforge-v${version}-linux-x64-glibc.tar.gz, SHA256SUMS and metadata-${version}.json. Neither the manifest nor the metadata mentions the .tar.gz.
reproduction: Local /tmp probe (no compile): checksums({sha256:'b'*64,...}) returns "bbbb...bbbb  swarmforge\n". Synthesized the exact 3-file release-asset directory and ran 'sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS' -> exit 1, 'swarmforge: FAILED open or read' / 'No such file or directory'; grep -c 'tar.gz' over SHA256SUMS and metadata-1.2.3.json -> 0 and 0.
recommendation: Emit an archive-level digest during packaging (add a swarmforge-v${version}-linux-x64-glibc.tar.gz entry to dist/SHA256SUMS, or write dist/<archive>.sha256), attach it in the gh release create step, and have prepareReleaseAssets re-check the downloaded archive against it before the draft is created; reword the notes to distinguish 'verify the archive digest' from 'SHA256SUMS verifies the extracted executable'.
confidence: high - reproduced locally for the manifest content and the failing sha256sum -c, and code-evidenced for the asset list
why_not_caught: verifyArchive (scripts/package.ts:158-251) and prepareReleaseAssets (:380-404) only prove things inside the tarball. tests/packaging.test.ts:763-836 asserts asset file names and :1000-1045 asserts workflow substrings; no test requires a published digest to cover the downloadable archive. README.md:51/63 is self-consistent (verification inside the extracted tree), so the gap is specific to the release notes wording plus the missing archive digest.

title: Third-party action pinned to a mutable tag runs inside the only job holding contents: write, after the write-scoped token was persisted on disk
evidence: release.yml:118-119 grants contents: write to draft-release; :121-123 checkout@v4 sets no persist-credentials (default true, so the job token is written to .git/config as an http.https://github.com/.extraheader basic-auth header); :125-127 then runs oven-sh/setup-bun@v2, a non-GitHub action pinned to a mutable tag. GH_TOKEN is only set on the final gh step, which does not contain the exposure because the token is already readable from .git/config by any later step.
reproduction: Not reproducible locally; requires the upstream v2 tag to be moved or compromised. Code-evidenced from the workflow text at the exact target (quoted above). No attempt was made to contact or influence upstream.
recommendation: Pin third-party (and ideally actions/*) refs to a full 40-hex commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment, and add persist-credentials: false to the draft-release checkout so the write-scoped token is not left in .git/config for later steps.
confidence: medium-high - code-evidenced workflow configuration; the compromise precondition is unverified
why_not_caught: tests/packaging.test.ts:932-953 only asserts that contents: write and github.token do not appear in the build job; it asserts nothing about action pinning or credential persistence, and no step sets persist-credentials: false.

title: Workflow definition is taken from the tagged commit, so the draft-only gate is not a trusted boundary
evidence: on: push: tags 'v*' accepts a tag on any ref. The only gates are the event-name check (:45, :115) and 'bun scripts/package.ts tag' (:48, :132), both inside the workflow file that GitHub loads from the tagged commit. Nothing requires the tagged commit to be reachable from the protected default branch; no github.ref_protected check, no environment approval, no separate trusted-definer workflow.
reproduction: Code-evidenced control flow; not executed (would require publishing a release, which this review must not do). A collaborator with branch-write access could tag a branch commit whose release.yml drops --draft, turning branch write into an immediate published release - and README.md:34-57 documents releases as the install channel, so installers would fetch attacker binaries from a trusted release page. The package.ts tag version check does not defend this: it lives in the same attacker-supplied workflow file.
recommendation: Add a repository ruleset / tag-protection rule requiring release tags to target commits reachable from the protected default branch; as defense in depth gate draft-release on 'if: github.ref_protected == true' (or verify github.sha is contained in the default branch) and put the write step behind a protected environment with required reviewers.
confidence: medium - workflow-level behaviour is code-evidenced, but reachability depends on repository rulesets, tag protection and default workflow permissions that were not inspected (read-only review, no infrastructure calls). Mitigated at the platform layer if tag protection is configured.
why_not_caught: tests/packaging.test.ts:1000-1045 asserts '--draft' present and '--publish' absent in the file at the reviewed commit; it cannot constrain the file at an arbitrary tag.

title: Published SHA256SUMS/metadata are the loose top-level copies, never digest-compared with the copies inside the verified archive
evidence: verifyArchive checks the manifest and metadata extracted from the tarball; prepareReleaseAssets (:388-390) resolves the loose files by recursive findFile and returns them as 'assets', and release.yml:157-159 attaches exactly those paths. The loose copies are never compared with the archive's own copies.
reproduction: Code trace only - not demonstrated reachable. packageCli writes both copies from the same in-memory content (:303-304 then :315-319) and the build job uploads a single artifact, so they are identical today.
recommendation: Have prepareReleaseAssets read the manifest and metadata out of the verified archive and compare digests with the loose copies before returning them as assets.
confidence: low - explicitly an unverified hypothesis / hardening gap, not a live bug
why_not_caught: No test asserts the loose and in-archive copies agree; the current construction makes them identical.

title: Quickstart tells the operator to create .env, but no supported entry point loads it
evidence: README.md:9 instructs `cp .env.example .env` and fill six values, then README.md:12 shows plain `bun run dev` and README.md:26 says production starts with `bun start`. package.json:10-13 makes every script `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null src/cli.ts ...` and scripts/package.ts:106 sets autoload_dotenv:false for the compiled binary, so Bun never loads .env. src/main.ts:7 calls resolveServerSettings() with no options, so only a config file (src/settings/paths.ts:58), its env_file, an explicit --env-file, or the process environment is read (src/settings/load.ts:738-762). The corrected form appears only later, at README.md:17-22.
reproduction: Reproduced with Bun 1.4.2 in a /tmp copy of the target. With a filled .env in the checkout cwd: `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null src/cli.ts serve --check-config` exits 1 with 'Invalid configuration: FREESTYLE_API_TOKEN ... SWARMFORGE_GIT_TREE: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined'. Adding `--env-file .env` exits 0 with ok:true. Consequence: the documented first-run and production commands cannot start the server. tests/packaging.test.ts:851 only asserts the scripts contain --no-env-file and :871 tests the corrected --env-file form; no test parses README.md:9 or :12.
recommendation: Change README.md:9 and README.md:26 to `bun run start -- --env-file .env` (or exported values), and correct docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:3 ('Bun loads `.env`'), which is false for every supported entry point.

title: docs/ENVIRONMENT.md still publishes the replaced SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH default; silent new-database cutover
evidence: ENVIRONMENT.md:31 documents the default as `./data/swarmforge.sqlite`. src/settings/load.ts:835-841 sets the key to defaultDatabasePath() (src/settings/paths.ts:66-72) = $XDG_DATA_HOME/swarmforge/... when absolute, else ~/.local/share/swarmforge/swarmforge.sqlite. The old value survives only as loadConfig's zod default (src/config.ts:77), which the resolver always overrides. CONFIGURATION.md:130-131 states the XDG default 'replaces the environment-only default ./data/swarmforge.sqlite', and CONFIGURATION.md:3 claims ENVIRONMENT.md 'stays valid', yet this branch did not update ENVIRONMENT.md (diff vs base 5672ead touches README, CONFIGURATION.md, SERVE.md, package.json, scripts only).
reproduction: Reproduced: with no SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH set and an isolated HOME, `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null src/cli.ts config show` exits 0 and reports SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH=<HOME>/.local/share/swarmforge/swarmforge.sqlite with source 'default'. Consequence for an existing deployment that relied on the documented default: the server silently opens a new empty database, all worker rows/results/instance history disappear, and nothing refuses the cutover because the instance-ID ownership check (startup step 3 in docs/SERVE.md) passes against the new empty file. tests/settings.test.ts:169-184 asserts the new default, so code and tests agree and only the doc cell is stale.
recommendation: Update the ENVIRONMENT.md:31 default cell to the XDG value with its ~ / absolute note, and add a short migration warning there; optionally add a test asserting documented defaults match the resolver.

title: Documented systemd unit omits WorkingDirectory while the shipped db_path is relative
evidence: The unit at README.md:95-101 sets only Type/ExecStart/TimeoutStopSec/Restart - no WorkingDirectory - and passes only --env-file. .env.example:36 ships `SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH=./data/swarmforge.sqlite`, a relative path. src/settings/load.ts:796-804 anchors an env-file host_path at prepared.cwd (the invocation directory, docs/CONFIGURATION.md:132-134), and src/store.ts:19 does mkdirSync(dirname(path), {recursive:true}) before opening SQLite. systemd's default working directory is `/`.
reproduction: Anchoring reproduced: `serve --check-config --env-file ./secrets.env` run from an empty directory exits 0 and resolves SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH=<cwd>/data/swarmforge.sqlite. The systemd cwd=/ case is code-evidenced, not executed. Consequence: the database lands at /data/swarmforge.sqlite (created as root), silently splitting the deployment, or startup fails with EACCES for a non-root User= and exits 1 (src/serve-command.ts:175-180). src/cli.ts:194-201 (--check-config) can report the anchored path but the README never tells the operator to run it for the unit; tests/settings.test.ts:391-404 pins the anchoring as intended.
recommendation: Add WorkingDirectory= (and User=) to the README unit, and note beside .env.example:36 that the relative default resolves against the process working directory so services should set an absolute path.

title: ENVIRONMENT.md still asserts 'Bun loads .env'

evidence: Two mutations, each run against the only suite importing these modules (tests/packaging.test.ts), each 35 pass / 0 fail: (1) scripts/build.ts:182 `compileCli()` replaced with a literal stub object -> 35 pass. title: Artifact listing symlink-kind filter is dead to the suite: removing it leaves the full suite green
evidence: Deleting the single line `e.kind !== "symlink" &&` -> full suite 262 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail. FreestyleProvider.listFiles (src/providers/freestyle.ts:308-310) passes the SDK DirEntry through unchanged, and node_modules/freestyle/dist/vms/types.d.ts:449-453 documents kind as `file | directory | symlink`. evidence: code-evidenced: triggers are `on: push: tags: [v*]` and `workflow_dispatch` only (.github/workflows/release.yml:7-11). `find .github -type f` shows this is the repository's only workflow, and its `Test` and `Static checks` steps live inside the release job, gated on a tag already existing.

title: Redactor re-reads the whole worker table and rescans every string once per secret, blocking the single-threaded event loop
evidence: redactorFor() (src/security.ts:43-50) returns a lazy secrets() closure over c.store.all(); Redactor.text() (src/security.ts:5-23) calls this.secrets() on EVERY invocation, then runs (3+workers)*3 String.replaceAll passes (1209 at 400 workers). value() (src/security.ts:24-37) recurses per string field, so an N-field response performs N full-table scans of workers plus JSON.parse per row. Hot callers: src/coordinator.ts:650-651 (per worker per poll), src/coordinator.ts:707, src/runtime.ts:185,198 (per event per 1s flush), src/mcp.ts:40 (every tool response), src/http.ts:42, src/files.ts:70,103,135.
reproduction: REPRODUCED with Bun 1.4.2, real SQLite under /tmp, fake provider/agent; probes in /tmp/sfrev/probe (disclosed). list_workers page of 100, response redaction only: 79.4ms @50 workers, 474.9ms @200, 1013.5ms @400. One coordinator.tick() (5 assistant msgs/snapshot, stable excerpt text): 33.7ms @50, 68.5 @100, 268.7 @200, 821.3 @400 (superlinear). eventLogger first flush (1600 pending events, 100 per pass): 1291.5ms at 400 workers, against setInterval(flush,1000) at src/serve.ts:193.
recommendation: Materialize the secret set once (refresh on worker create / config load) and pass it into text(); replace the 3-variant replaceAll loop with one prebuilt alternation regex; at minimum hoist secrets() out of text() into value() so one response costs one scan, not N.

title: /metrics render is O(workers x events) because events.worker_id has no index; each scrape stalls the event loop
evidence: The for (const w of all) loop at src/metrics.ts:81 issues three full-table events scans per worker per scrape: GROUP BY type (:100-104), min(at) for worker.ready (:111-115), and per-completed-dispatch lookup using json_extract(data,'$.run_id') (:121-129). Schema src/store.ts:27 declares no index on events.worker_id; only workers_state (:26) and dispatch_worker (:29) exist.
reproduction: REPRODUCED. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN at target returns ["SCAN events","USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY"] for the per-worker GROUP BY. Metrics.render() timing: 9.1ms @50 workers (250 event rows), 67.9ms @200 (1000 rows), 253.6ms @400 (2000 rows). Only 5 events per worker were created; a long-lived deployment accumulates far more, and cost grows linearly from these points.
recommendation: Add CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_worker_type ON events(worker_id,type,at) to src/store.ts; replace the per-worker loop with per-team GROUP BY aggregations; store run_id as an events column instead of filtering with json_extract(data,'$.run_id').

title: No concurrency cap on provider/agent fan-out: hundreds of simultaneous outbound TLS connections
evidence: runTick dispatches Promise.allSettled over every non-terminal, non-paused, non-queued worker (src/coordinator.ts:340-352) each SWARMFORGE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS; runRecover dispatches Promise.all over every worker with a vm_id (src/coordinator.ts:397-400) each 30s reconcile and at startup. exclusive() (src/coordinator.ts:266-271) serializes per worker ID only and imposes no cross-worker bound. FreestyleProvider (src/providers/freestyle.ts:20-24) only attaches a per-request AbortSignal.timeout; there is no semaphore, retry budget or 429 handling. SWARMFORGE_MAX_WORKERS has no upper bound in the config schema.
reproduction: REPRODUCED with an instrumented fake provider: Coordinator.recover() with 400 workers returned provider_getWorker_calls=400 and peak_concurrent_provider_requests=400 (recover_ms 52.7 at 20ms fake latency). The provider-side effect (rate limits, socket exhaustion) is code-evidenced only; no real provider was contacted.
recommendation: Route provider/agent calls in runTick and runRecover through a bounded concurrency pool (16-32), and treat provider 429/5xx as backpressure (skip the tick) instead of recording it as a worker error.

title: OpenCode session history is refetched in full on every poll and every historical assistant message re-upserts usage
evidence: OpenCodeAgent.inspect() loops `while (page.length === 100)` (src/providers/opencode.ts:116-129), issuing sequential older-page requests until a short page, on every poll for every running/waiting worker. monitor() then calls store.usage() once per assistant message in the snapshot on every poll (src/coordinator.ts:544-554), even when the max() upsert is a value no-op.
reproduction: PARTIALLY REPRODUCED. SQLite side measured with a fake agent: coordinator.tick() at 400 workers x 60 assistant messages per snapshot = 359.5ms of write bookkeeping with the excerpt path disabled. The HTTP page fan-out was not exercised (fake agent returns the snapshot directly), so ceil(history/100) sequential round trips per worker per poll is code-evidenced only. At 400 workers with a 250-message session that is 1200 requests per 2s tick plus ~100k UPSERTs, on top of the redaction cost in finding 1.
recommendation: Fetch only messages newer than the highest message id already recorded for the worker, or bound inspect() to the current dispatch's message subtree; skip the usage() write when the stored row already holds equal or greater totals.

title: store.all() full-table scan with JSON.parse per row, called twice per tick and once per spawn
evidence: all() is SELECT body FROM workers ORDER BY rowid with JSON.parse per row (src/store.ts). runTick scans twice (src/coordinator.ts:316 and :363); spawn() scans once per spawn for queue depth and the request_id retry check (src/coordinator.ts:172); metrics and MCP status tools scan again (src/metrics.ts:74, src/mcp.ts:262,277).
reproduction: REPRODUCED in isolation: store.all() 0.35ms at 50 rows, 1.68ms at 400 rows. Individually minor; it is the multiplier that makes findings 1 and 3 expensive.
recommendation: Project only the columns each caller needs, reuse one snapshot per tick, and compute queue depth/capacity in SQL.

title: runRecover does an O(VMs x workers) linear scan for VM ownership
evidence: For each VM returned by provider.listWorkers(), runRecover runs all.find((w) => w.vm_id === vm.id) over the full worker array (src/coordinator.ts:373-377), i.e. 160,000 comparisons at 400 VMs and 400 workers, every 30s reconcile. The same function already builds a byId Map for the fallback lookup one line later, so this is an oversight rather than a constraint.
reproduction: CODE-EVIDENCED. The nested loop is unambiguous in the source; not separately benchmarked because the cost is far below findings 1-3.
recommendation: Build a Map<vm_id, worker_id> alongside byId and use it for both lookups.
